functions.name: AdjustBoundsAndRenderWindowRegion
functions.signature: void AdjustBoundsAndRenderWindowRegion(HWND hWindow, HRGN hRegion, int nClipX, int nClipY, int nClipWidth, RECT * pBounds, int * pOutput, uint dwColorParam1, uint dwColorParam2, uint dwColorParam3)
functions.comment:
Adjusts rectangular bounds and delegates to compositing window renderer.
Algorithm: 1. Load pBounds parameter. 2. Allocate stack space. 3. Test if pBounds is non-NULL. 4. If NULL, skip adjustment. 5. If valid, extract x, y, width, height from bounds structure. 6. Increment width and height by 1. 7. Store adjusted bounds on stack. 8. Call RenderWindowRegionWithCompositing with all parameters. 9. Clean up stack and return.
Parameters: hWindow (HWND) - Target window handle. hRegion (HRGN) - Region handle for clipping. nClipX (int) - Clip rectangle X coordinate. nClipY (int) - Clip rectangle Y coordinate. nClipWidth (int) - Clip rectangle width. pBounds (RECT *) - Pointer to bounds or NULL. pOutput (int *) - Output buffer pointer. dwColorParam1 (uint) - Color parameter 1. dwColorParam2 (uint) - Color parameter 2. dwColorParam3 (uint) - Color parameter 3.
Returns: void - No return value; delegates rendering to RenderWindowRegionWithCompositing which handles all output.

functions.name: RegisterDialogClasses
functions.comment:
Registers two dialog window classes for the custom dialog system.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize WNDCLASSA structure for SDlgDialog class
   - Set style to CS_DLGFRAME (0x8)
   - Set window procedure to ProcessDialogWindowMessage
   - Set extra window bytes to 0x1e (30 bytes for dialog instance data)
   - Load arrow cursor via LoadCursorA(NULL, IDC_ARROW)
   - Call RegisterClassA to register SDlgDialog class
   - Return FALSE immediately if registration fails
2. Query system Static class information using GetClassInfoA
3. Modify Static class to create SDlgStatic custom class
   - Clear CS_VREDRAW flag from style (AND with 0xffffff7f mask)
   - Set window procedure to DialogControlWindowProc
   - Load arrow cursor via LoadCursorA(NULL, IDC_ARROW)
   - Set background brush to white via GetStockObject(WHITE_BRUSH)
   - Register modified class as SDlgStatic
4. Return TRUE if both registrations succeeded, FALSE if either failed
5. Set global initialization flag g_dwDialogClassesInitialized to 1

Parameters:
None

Returns:
bool - TRUE if both window classes registered successfully, FALSE if registration fails

Special Cases:
- If SDlgDialog registration fails, function returns immediately without attempting SDlgStatic
- Static class information must be queried from Windows system before modification
- CS_VREDRAW flag (0x00000080) explicitly removed from Static class to prevent redraw flashing
- Both classes use extra window bytes for instance data (0x1e = 30 bytes)
- Uses standard Windows API: GetModuleHandleA, GetClassInfoA, LoadCursorA, RegisterClassA, GetStockObject
- Arrow cursor identifier IDC_ARROW is loaded as 0x7f00 (magic constant from Windows)
- White background brush obtained via GetStockObject(1)

Structure Layout - WNDCLASSA:
Offset  Size  Field Name        Type           Description
0       2     style             unsigned int   Window class style flags (CS_DLGFRAME=0x8)
2       4     lpfnWndProc       WNDPROC        Pointer to window procedure function
6       4     cbClsExtra        int            Extra class bytes (0 for both classes)
10      4     cbWndExtra        int            Extra window bytes (0x1e=30 for SDlgDialog)
14      4     hInstance         HINSTANCE      Module instance handle from GetModuleHandleA
18      4     hIcon             HICON          Icon handle (NULL for both)
22      4     hCursor           HCURSOR        Cursor from LoadCursorA(IDC_ARROW)
26      4     hbrBackground     HBRUSH         Background brush (white for SDlgStatic)
30      4     lpszMenuName      LPCSTR         Menu resource name (NULL)
34      4     lpszClassName     LPCSTR         Pointer to class name string
Total:  40 bytes

String References:
- szSDlgDialogClassName (0x6fc3756c): Contains "SDlgDialog" for primary dialog class
- szStaticClassName (0x6fc37564): Contains "Static" for Windows system Static class query
- szSDlgStaticClassName (0x6fc37558): Contains "SDlgStatic" for custom static control class

Global References:
- g_dwDialogClassesInitialized (0x6fc453b8): Set to 1 after class registration starts

functions.name: ShowModalDialog
functions.signature: HANDLE ShowModalDialog(HINSTANCE hInstance, int * pDialogTemplate, HWND hParentWindow, LPVOID pDialogProc, LPARAM lParam)
functions.comment:
Display a modal dialog box with parent window management.

Displays a dialog modally, ensuring parent window is disabled during dialog interaction
and restored afterward. Manages dialog lifecycle from creation through message processing
to cleanup, returning the dialog result code to the caller.

Algorithm:
1. Check if dialog window classes are registered; register if needed
2. Create dialog window from template with callback procedure
3. If parent window specified and not desktop window, disable parent and set modal flag
4. Enter message processing loop: continuously check SDlg_EndDialog property
5. Process pending window messages until dialog signals termination
6. Retrieve dialog result code from SDlg_EndResult property
7. Clean up all dialog properties (SDlg_Modal, SDlg_EndDialog, SDlg_EndResult)
8. Destroy dialog window and restore parent window enabled state
9. Return dialog result code to caller

Parameters:
- hInstance: Module instance handle for loading dialog template resource
- pDialogTemplate: Pointer to dialog template structure defining dialog layout and controls
- hParentWindow: Parent window handle; if null, no parent; if desktop, skip modality
- pDialogProc: Dialog procedure callback function for processing dialog messages
- lParam: Additional parameter passed to dialog procedure on initialization

Returns:
- Dialog result code from EndDialog (set via SDlg_EndResult property)
- 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) on failure: class registration failed or dialog creation failed

Special Cases:
- Minimized parent window (iconic) is not disabled during modality
- Desktop window is detected via GetDesktopWindow and skipped for modality
- Dialog properties use string keys for interprocess compatibility
- Message loop uses property-based signaling for thread-safe termination

functions.name: InitializeDialogWithClasses
functions.signature: void InitializeDialogWithClasses(HINSTANCE hInstance, int * pDialogResource, HWND hParentWindow, LPVOID pDialogData, LPARAM lParamExtra)
functions.comment:
Initializes and registers dialog control classes, then creates a modeless dialog window.

Algorithm:
1. Load global registration flag (g_dwDialogClassesInitialized) from address 0x6fc453b8
2. Test EAX against zero to check if dialog classes have already been registered
3. If classes already registered (EAX != 0), jump to skip_registration label
4. Call RegisterDialogClasses() at 0x6fc11220 to register custom control window classes
5. Test EAX result to check registration success (EAX != 0 means success)
6. If registration failed (EAX == 0), return immediately with RET 0x14
7. If registration succeeded, continue to skip_registration label
8. Call CreateDialogWithControls() at 0x6fc0df90 to create and display the dialog
9. Return to caller using RET 0x14 (callee cleanup of 5 parameters)

Parameters:
hInstance: HINSTANCE - Module instance handle for locating dialog template resources
pDialogResource: int * - Pointer to dialog template resource or resource ID constant
hParentWindow: HWND - Parent window handle for dialog ownership and initial positioning
pDialogData: LPVOID - Initialization data pointer passed to dialog message handler procedures
lParamExtra: LPARAM - Extra parameter passed during dialog creation and initialization

Returns:
void - Creates modeless dialog window if registration succeeds; returns without creating if
registration fails. Dialog persists after function returns.

Special Cases:
- Singleton registration pattern: Custom control classes registered only once (tracked by
  g_dwDialogClassesInitialized global flag at 0x6fc453b8)
- Early exit on failure: If RegisterDialogClasses() returns EAX=0 (failure), function exits
  immediately without calling CreateDialogWithControls()
- Calling convention __stdcall: Callee responsible for stack cleanup; RET 0x14 removes
  5 parameters (hInstance=4, pDialogResource=4, hParentWindow=4, pDialogData=4, lParamExtra=4)

functions.name: ShowResourceModalDialog
functions.signature: int ShowResourceModalDialog(void * hModule, char * pResourceName, void * hwndParent, void * pDialogData, int lParamExtra)
functions.comment:
Loads a resource from a module and displays it as a modal dialog

Algorithm:
1. Call FindResourceA to locate the resource by name in the specified module
2. If FindResourceA returns NULL, jump to resource_not_found and return NULL
3. Call LoadResource to load the located resource into memory
4. If LoadResource returns NULL, jump to load_resource_failed and return NULL
5. Call LockResource to obtain memory address of the loaded resource
6. If LockResource succeeds (non-zero), continue to show dialog step
7. Call ShowModalDialog with locked resource pointer and dialog parameters
8. Return dialog result from ShowModalDialog (EAX contains result)
9. If any step fails, return NULL to indicate failure

Parameters:
hModule - Handle to module/DLL containing the resource
pResourceName - Pointer to resource name string to locate
hwndParent - Parent window handle for modal dialog positioning
pDialogData - Optional pointer to data passed to dialog procedure
lParamExtra - Additional parameter passed to dialog procedure

Returns:
INT_PTR - Dialog result if successful, NULL if resource not found or load failed

functions.name: ComputeAllocationBlockMetadata
functions.comment:
Calculates memory block allocation metadata and size differences.

Algorithm:
1. Test allocation type flag (bit 0x4) in header flags byte at offset +0x3
2. If allocation type flag set: load size from parameter stack at offset -0x10, add 0x1c (28 bytes) overhead, store result
3. If flag not set: load size byte from header offset +0x2, add 0x8 (8 bytes) base overhead, store result
4. Test additional size flag (bit 0x1) in header flags byte at offset +0x3
5. If additional flag set: add 0x2 more bytes to the computed allocation size
6. Load 16-bit header word at offset +0x0 and compute difference from calculated size
7. Store size difference in output result array for validation and bounds checking

Parameters:
pMemoryHeader (Stack[0x4]): Pointer to MemoryBlockHeader with flags and size fields
pSizeResultArray (Stack[0x8]): Pointer to int array storing offset 0, difference at offset 5/6

Returns:
void - Results stored in pSizeResultArray: index 0 for intermediate offset, index 5/6 for size difference

Special Cases:
- Allocation type flag 0x4: Triggers alternate calculation with 0x1c overhead and -0x10 stack access
- Additional size flag 0x1: Adds 2 bytes when set, used for extended allocation headers
- Header validation: Size difference used to verify allocation metadata consistency
- Magic values: 0x8 base overhead, 0x1c flagged overhead, 0x2 extra conditional overhead

functions.name: DequeueAndFreeLinkedListNode
functions.comment:
Dequeue the first node from a linked list and release its memory.

Algorithm:
1. Load the current node pointer from the list head reference
2. Load the next pointer from the current node's first field
3. Update the list head to point to the next node (dequeue operation)
4. Call VirtualFree with MEM_RELEASE flag to free the current node's memory

Parameters:
- pListHead (__fastcall in ECX): Pointer to a pointer that holds the list head address. Points to a structure where the first field is a pointer to the next node. Modified to point to the next node after dequeue.

Returns:
- void: No return value. The list head is modified in-place via the pointer.

Special Cases:
- The function assumes pListHead points to valid memory containing a pointer
- The pointed-to node must have a valid next pointer at offset +0x0
- Memory is released with VirtualFree using MEM_RELEASE (0x8000) flag with zero size
- No validation is performed; passing invalid pointers will cause an access violation

Structure Layout:
List nodes are assumed to follow this pattern:
  Offset  Size  Field Name     Type      Description
  ------  ----  ----------     ----      -----------
  +0x0    4     nextNode       void*     Pointer to the next node in the linked list

functions.name: InitializePageSizeAlignment
functions.comment:
Initializes system page alignment size for memory allocator.
Queries the system page size and finds the smallest power-of-2 value >= page size.
This alignment value is stored globally for use by memory allocation functions.
Algorithm: Call GetSystemInfo, initialize alignment to 1, loop doubling until >= page size.
Parameters: None - operates on system page size via Windows API.
Returns: void - result stored in g_dwPageAlignmentSize global variable.

functions.name: CalculateAlignedBufferSize
functions.signature: void CalculateAlignedBufferSize(uint nSize, int * pIsConfigured, int * pAlignedSize, int * pPadding, int * pIsAllowed)
functions.comment:
Calculate aligned buffer size with configuration-dependent padding.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwConfigBit2 global configuration flag
2. Compare input nSize against threshold 0xfe88 (65160 bytes)
3. Set isConfigured = 1 if g_dwConfigBit2 is set OR nSize >= 0xfe88, else 0
4. Write isConfigured value to *pIsConfigured output pointer
5. Load g_dwConfigBit0 global allowed flag from address 0x6fc44d5c
6. Set isAllowed = 1 only if g_dwConfigBit0 is set AND isConfigured is 0, else 0
7. Write isAllowed value to *pIsAllowed output pointer
8. If isConfigured is set, add 4 to nSize for offset calculation purposes
9. Calculate intermediate value: (isAllowed ? 2 : 0) + 8 + nSize
10. Calculate final aligned size by rounding to 8-byte boundary via bitwise operations
11. Calculate padding bytes as difference between aligned size and intermediate value
12. Write alignedSize and padding values to output pointers

Parameters:
  nSize: Input buffer size (uint), compared against 0xfe88 threshold for configuration
  pIsConfigured: Pointer to output isConfigured flag (0 or 1)
  pAlignedSize: Pointer to output final 8-byte aligned buffer size
  pPadding: Pointer to output padding bytes needed for alignment
  pIsAllowed: Pointer to output isAllowed flag (1 if allowed bit set and not configured)

Returns:
  void - function writes results to four output pointer parameters only

Special Cases:
  Size Threshold: 0xfe88 (65160 decimal) determines configuration state
  Offset Addition: If isConfigured, size increased by 4 bytes before alignment
  Alignment Boundary: Always 8-byte alignment using (-value & 7) bitwise operation
  Allow Flag: Only true when both global bit 0 is set AND isConfigured is false

functions.name: ComputeCappedShiftIndex
functions.comment:
Computes a capped shifted index value by right-shifting input by 5 bits with maximum cap of 8.

Algorithm:
1. Right-shift EAX input value by 5 bits (equivalent to divide by 32)
2. Compare shifted result against cap value of 8
3. If result is less than or equal to 8, jump to return
4. If result is greater than 8, set EAX to cap value of 8
5. Return capped result in EAX

Parameters:
IMPLICIT EAX - dwInputValue: Input value to be shifted and capped

Returns:
EAX - dwCappedResult: Capped shifted result (range 0-8, where each unit represents 32 in the input value)

Special Cases:
- Cap value is 8 (0x8), preventing overflow
- Right shift by 5 bits (0x5) = division by 32
- Input range 0-255 produces output 0-7
- Input range 256+ produces output capped at 8

functions.name: RebuildAllocatorFreeLists
functions.comment: Setting prototype: void RebuildAllocatorFreeLists(void * pAllocator)

functions.name: EnterHeapIndexCriticalSection
functions.comment:
Enters critical section for heap and returns the shifted heap index.

Algorithm:
1. Extract heap index from input handle at EAX+0x4: Load ushort, left-shift by 16 bits
2. Load heap pointer from array at offset (dwHeapIndexShifted + 0x8)
3. Calculate critical section offset: heapPointer * 0x18 from base g_PoolCriticalSections
4. Call EnterCriticalSection with calculated offset for thread-safe access
5. Store heap pointer to output parameter *pHeapPointerOut
6. Return shifted heap index in EAX

Parameters:
pHeapPointerOut (uint*): Output pointer to receive heap pointer value

Returns:
uint: Shifted heap index (ushort from EAX+0x4 << 16) for LeaveCriticalSection call

Special Cases:
- Heap index created by left-shifting ushort by 16 bits (0x10000 multiply)
- Critical section array g_PoolCriticalSections has 0x18 byte stride
- Implicit parameter: Heap handle in EAX register on function entry
- Caller must invoke LeaveCriticalSection with returned index when done

functions.name: ExtractStatusByte
functions.comment:
Extracts the lowest byte from a status value via bitwise AND mask.

Algorithm:
1. Apply bitwise AND with 0xFF mask to the input parameter in EAX
2. Return the masked byte value

Parameters:
  status - Input status value (passed in EAX, extracted as byte)

Returns:
  unsigned char - The lowest byte of the input (0x00-0xFF)

Purpose:
This utility function isolates the least significant byte from a status or flag value,
effectively truncating any higher byte values and returning only the byte portion.
Commonly used for extracting status codes or flags from packed data.

functions.name: ResolveConditionalPointer
functions.comment:
Resolves a conditional pointer value from an object structure with optional dereferencing.

Algorithm:
1. Test if the input object pointer (ECX) is null
2. Return NULL if null pointer detected
3. Calculate effective address at offset +8 from object base (pointer field location)
4. Test bit 2 of the byte at offset +3 to determine if dereferencing is required
5. If indirection flag is set, dereference the pointer at offset +8 to get the final target
6. Return the resolved pointer value in EAX (either direct or dereferenced)

Parameters:
- pObject (ECX): Pointer to object structure with conditional pointer field
  - Offset +3: Byte containing flags (bit 2 = indirection mode)
  - Offset +8: Pointer value (direct target or pointer-to-pointer)

Returns:
- void*: Resolved pointer address, or NULL if input is null
  - Direct pointer if indirection flag not set
  - Dereferenced pointer if indirection flag is set
  - NULL for null input

Special Cases:
- Null input handling: immediate NULL return without field access
- Bit 2 at offset +3 controls pointer dereferencing behavior
- Used for polymorphic data structures with conditional indirection

functions.name: LoadIndexedValue
functions.comment:
Loads a value from an indexed location within a large data table.

Algorithm:
1. Load unsigned 16-bit index value from parameter structure at offset +4
2. Scale index by 64KB (0x10000 / 65536 bytes) by left-shifting 16 bits
3. Load 32-bit value from the scaled offset location at +4
4. Return the loaded value

Parameters:
  pBaseAddress - Pointer to structure containing index field at offset +4

Returns:
  int - 32-bit value loaded from scaled index location

Special Cases:
  - Index multiplied by 65536 (0x10000) suggests accessing large table with 64KB strides
  - Actual data table address calculated as (index * 65536) + 4
  - No input validation - caller must ensure valid pointer and reasonable index

functions.name: GetMemoryMetadata
functions.comment:
Retrieves metadata from a heap allocation with a hidden header structure.

Algorithm:
1. Test if pMemory pointer is NULL; if so, return 0 immediately
2. Load flag byte from offset -5 of the original pointer
3. Adjust pointer backward by 8 bytes
4. Test bit 0x8 in the flag byte to check if hidden metadata is available
5. If flag is set, load and return the hidden value from offset -0xc (4 bytes before adjusted pointer)
6. If flag is not set, return the adjusted pointer value instead
7. Return result via EAX and exit

Parameters:
- pMemory (EAX/Stack[0x4]): Pointer to user data in heap allocation; actual metadata located at negative offsets from this address

Returns:
- EAX: Either the adjusted pointer (pMemory - 8) or the hidden metadata value from offset -0xc, depending on the 0x8 flag bit; returns 0 if pMemory is NULL

Special Cases:
- Magic value 0x8: Flag bit in byte at offset -5 indicates presence of hidden metadata
- Offset -0xc: Contains optional hidden metadata value (DWORD)
- Offset -5: Contains flag byte controlling metadata presence
- NULL pointer handling: Returns 0 without accessing memory

Structure Layout (Memory Header Before pMemory):
Offset | Size | Field       | Type  | Description
-------|------|-------------|-------|---------------------------------------------
-12    | 4    | hidden_data | dword | Optional metadata (returned if flag 0x8 set)
-8     | 4    | reserved    | dword | Reserved or alignment
-4     | 1    | padding     | byte  | Padding (not used)
-5     | 1    | flags       | byte  | Flag byte; bit 0x8 = hidden_data presence
0      | *    | user_data   | void  | User payload (pMemory points here)

functions.name: GetLastError
functions.comment:
Returns the last Storm error code.

Algorithm:
1. Read the global error code variable (g_dwLastError)
2. Return the value to caller

Parameters:
- None (void)

Returns:
- Last error code set by SetLastError or 0 if none

Related Functions:
- Ordinal_465: Sets the error code (SetLastError wrapper)

functions.name: InsertBlockIntoFreeList
functions.comment: Setting prototype: void InsertBlockIntoFreeList(int nAllocatorContext, int nBlockSizePtr)

functions.name: AllocateMemoryBlock
functions.signature: void AllocateMemoryBlock(void * pAllocator, int nCurrentBlockSize, uint nRequestedSize)
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a memory block within a custom allocator structure.

Algorithm:
1. Call CalculateAlignedBufferSize to compute alignment requirements and padding byte count
2. Load previous block flags from memory block header at offset +3
3. Clear bit 0 in previous flags (AND with 0xfe) to preserve state bits
4. Call InsertBlockIntoFreeList to manage freed memory blocks in size-based buckets
5. Store aligned block size in header word at offset +0
6. Store padding byte count in header at offset +2
7. Store combined flags byte (new allocation bit | preserved flags) at offset +3
8. Copy metadata field from allocator offset +0xc to block header offset +4
9. If padding needed: write sentinel value 0x12b1 at padding boundary offset
10. Update allocator total allocation counter at offset +0x18 with size difference

Parameters:
  pAllocator: Pointer to MemoryAllocator structure (offsets: +0xc metadata, +0x18 total, +0x20 endPtr, +0x38 freeLists)
  nCurrentBlockSize: Current block size or freed block size in bytes
  nRequestedSize: Requested allocation size in bytes (may differ from aligned size)

Returns:
  void - Modifies allocator state and block header in-place

Special Cases:
  Sentinel value 0x12b1 marks padding boundaries when alignment padding is needed
  Block flags byte uses bit 0 for allocation status, bits 1-6 for block type, bit 7 reserved
  Allocator maintains cumulative size tracking at offset +0x18 (unsigned DWORD)
  Free list insertion determines bucket based on calculated aligned size
  Configuration flags from CalculateAlignedBufferSize control padding strategy

Memory Block Header Layout (pBlockHeader at ESI):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type      Description
  0       2     blockSize       word      Aligned block size in bytes
  2       1     paddingBytes    byte      Number of padding bytes for alignment
  3       1     blockFlags      byte      Type (bits 1-6) and status (bit 0) flags
  4       4     metadata        dword     Copied from allocator configuration

Allocator Structure Fields:
  Offset  Size  Field          Type      Description
  0xc     4     metadata       dword     Configuration metadata copied to all blocks
  0x18    4     totalAlloc     dword     Cumulative allocation counter
  0x20    4     endPtr         pointer   End of current allocated region
  0x38    32    freeLists      dword[]   Array of 8 free list buckets indexed by size

functions.name: AllocateMemoryBlock
functions.signature: uint AllocateMemoryBlock(ushort * pBlockHeader, uint sizeRequested, uint sizeOriginal)
functions.comment:
Allocates a memory block from a custom memory allocator with gap handling and block consolidation.

Algorithm:
1. Calls CalculateAlignedBufferSize to compute aligned size, alignment, and error status for requested size
2. Returns 0 if alignment result exceeds 0xFFFF or alignment calculation failed
3. Determines memory gap between current block end (calculated from base + size stored in pBlockHeader[0])
4. If new block fits without gap, advances current block pointer and returns to finalization
5. If gap exists, iterates through linked free blocks starting at pBlockHeader[0]+alignment:
   - Accumulates free block sizes while checking block flags (bit 1 must be set for free block)
   - Stops if gap size is satisfied or reaches allocator limit
6. If gap insufficient, attempts to allocate new buffer memory (checks bounds at 0x2c/0x30 offsets)
7. Updates allocator state pointer at EBX+0x20 to mark gap boundaries
8. Inserts freed/compacted blocks back into free list and triggers memory compaction
9. Finalizes block header with size, alignment flags, and timestamp from EBX+0xc
10. Updates allocator statistics at EBX+0x18 with size difference
11. Returns 1 on success, 0 on any error condition (size overflow, allocation failure, bounds exceeded)

Parameters:
  pBlockHeader (ushort *): Pointer to block header [0]=current_size_offset, [1]=alignment_flags, [2-3]=metadata
  sizeRequested (uint): Requested allocation size in bytes  
  sizeOriginal (uint): Original size before alignment adjustment

Returns:
  uint: 1 if allocation successful, 0 if failed (overflow, bounds exceeded, alloc failed)

Special Cases:
  Magic marker 0x12b1 written at block boundary if alignment is applied
  Block flags at [base+3]: bit 1=free (0x2), bit 4=allocated (0x10)
  Gap consolidation iterates through linked blocks marked with 0x2 flag
  Allocator state pointer updated at EBX+0x20 to track gap boundaries
  Free block counter at EBX+0x24 decremented if blocks are consolidated
  Maximum block size limited to 0xFFFF (65535 bytes)

functions.name: DeallocateMemoryBlockFromPool
functions.comment:
Deallocates a memory block from a dynamic memory pool and updates pool state.

Algorithm:
1. Load block flags byte from EDI+3 and test allocated bit (0x4)
2. If allocated (0x4 set):
   a. Load allocation header pointer from EDI+8
   b. If header is not NULL, load allocation size from header-0x10
   c. Subtract size from pool allocation counter (ESI+0x34)
   d. Align address to page boundary using g_dwPageAlignmentSize
   e. Call VirtualFree to release page-aligned memory
3. If free block (0x4 not set):
   a. Load block size from EDI (word) and header size from EDI+2
   b. Calculate content size: block_size - header_size - 8
   c. If flag 0x1 set, subtract additional 2 bytes
4. Decrement block counter (ESI+0x14)
5. Subtract block size from pool used size (ESI+0x18)
6. Update block flags: clear 0x10, set 0x2 at EDI+3
7. Clear header size byte at EDI+2
8. Check if block is at pool end (EDI + size == ESI+0x20):
   a. If at end: Clear next pointer, update pool list head
   b. If not at end: Set bucket bit on next block, insert into free list
9. Calculate bucket index from block size >> 5 (cap at 8)
10. Update bucket list head (ESI+0x38 + bucket*4)
11. Increment free block counter if bucket bit or next block marked
12. If pool is empty (block_count == 0):
    a. Restore backup list head (ESI+0x1c to ESI+0x20)
    b. Clear all free list buckets (ESI+0x38 through ESI+0x58)
    c. Clear free block counter
    d. If no error flag, mark pool as available and set cleanup flag

Parameters:
  Implicit EDI = pointer to memory block header
  Implicit ESI = pointer to memory pool structure

Returns:
  void (no return value)

Special Cases:
  - Handles both allocated blocks (flag 0x4) and free blocks
  - VirtualFree called only if allocation header present
  - Segregated free list with size-based buckets (8 size categories)
  - Pool reset when last block removed (if no error)
  - Page alignment required for VirtualFree (4096-byte boundary)

Structure Layout - Memory Block Header:
  Offset  Size  Field Name     Type      Description
  0x0     2     block_size     word      Total block size in bytes
  0x2     1     header_size    byte      Header size code
  0x3     1     flags          byte      Bit 0x1=extra_bytes, 0x2=marked, 0x4=allocated, 0x10=bucket
  0x4     4     next_ptr       dword     Next block in linked list
  0x8     4     alloc_hdr      dword     Allocation header pointer (for allocated blocks)

Structure Layout - Memory Pool (minimum 0x5c bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field Name     Type      Description
  0x14    4     block_count    dword     Number of blocks in pool
  0x18    4     used_size      dword     Total bytes used by block data
  0x1c    4     backup_head    dword     Backup list head pointer
  0x20    4     list_head      dword     Current free/active list head
  0x24    4     free_count     dword     Free block counter
  0x34    4     alloc_size     dword     Total allocated memory size
  0x38    40    buckets[10]    dword     Free list buckets for size ranges

functions.name: ReportAndLogError
functions.comment:
Store the last error code and conditionally display error dialog if reporting is enabled.

Algorithm:
1. Save error code to global g_dwLastErrorCode for later retrieval
2. Call SetLastError to update Windows system error state
3. Load g_dwErrorReportingEnabled configuration flag
4. If reporting is disabled, skip error display and exit
5. If reporting is enabled, load error data pointer and error code from stack
6. Call DisplayErrorAndTerminate with 6 arguments: exit code (1), pointer argument (1), context (0), error data, error code, and exit code flag
7. Return to caller with stack cleanup (stdcall convention removes 8 bytes)

Parameters:
  pErrorData: uint * - Pointer to error information structure or buffer
  nErrorCode: int - Error code value to report and log

Returns:
  void - Function does not return a value, returns to caller

Special Cases:
  - If g_dwErrorReportingEnabled is 0, error display is skipped entirely
  - Error code is always stored to g_dwLastErrorCode before checking if display is needed
  - Uses __stdcall convention: callee removes 8 bytes of parameters from stack

functions.name: ComputeCachedStringHash
functions.comment:
Computes and caches string hash values with single-entry cache optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Load first dword from input string pointer (ESI) for cache comparison
2. Check if cache validity flag is set (g_dwCacheValidFlag != 0)
3. Compare current string pointer, hash flags, and first dword against cached values
4. If all three match, return cached hash value immediately (cache hit)
5. If cache miss or empty, clear the validity flag and proceed to compute
6. Skip hash computation if string pointer is null (ESI == 0)
7. Call ComputeStringHash(pString, 1, flags_implicit_ebx) with implicit registers
8. Clear sign bit from result (AND EAX, 0x7fffffff) to ensure positive hash
9. If computed hash is 0, set to 1 (guarantee non-zero return value)
10. Store computed hash, string pointer, flags, and first dword in cache
11. Set cache validity flag and return hash value

Parameters (Implicit Registers):
ESI (IMPLICIT): Pointer to null-terminated string buffer or NULL
EBX (IMPLICIT): Hash flags/options (passed through to ComputeStringHash)

Returns:
EAX: Non-zero hash value with sign bit cleared, range [1..0x7fffffff]

Special Cases:
- NULL pointer (ESI=0): Returns 1 without computing hash
- Hash result is 0: Clamped to 1 to guarantee non-zero return value
- Single-entry cache: Optimizes repeated hashing of identical string+flags combinations

functions.name: ComputeHashIfSystemInitialized
functions.comment:
Computes cached string hash value after verifying system initialization state.

Algorithm:
1. Load initialization flag from g_dwGameState (address 0x6fc45168)
2. If flag is zero (uninitialized):
   a. Set error code 0x8510007d to g_dwLastErrorCode (address 0x6fc45388)
   b. Call SetLastError(0x8510007d) via g_pfnSetLastError (address 0x6fc331fc)
   c. Load error reporting config flag from g_dwErrorReportingEnabled (address 0x6fc44d58)
   d. If error reporting enabled: call DisplayErrorAndTerminate with error details
   e. Return 0 to indicate error
3. If flag is non-zero (initialized):
   a. Load param1 into EBX (first parameter)
   b. Load param2 into ESI (second parameter)
   c. Call ComputeCachedStringHash() at address 0x6fc0ad80
   d. Return computed hash value from EAX

Parameters:
param1 (uint) - First parameter passed on stack via __stdcall convention
param2 (uint) - Second parameter passed on stack via __stdcall convention

Returns:
uint - Computed hash value on success, 0 on error (uninitialized state)

Special Cases:
Error Code: 0x8510007d indicates initialization check failure
Error Display: DisplayErrorAndTerminate called only if g_dwErrorReportingEnabled is set
Stack Cleanup: RET 0x8 cleans 2 parameters from stack (8 bytes total)

Calling Convention: __stdcall (parameters on stack, callee cleanup)

functions.name: SearchItemByHash
functions.signature: int SearchItemByHash(uint itemHash, int * pItemId, int * pItemData)
functions.comment:
Searches for an item in the global hash table by its item hash value.

Algorithm:
1. Check if memory heap is initialized; return 0 if not
2. Validate output parameters are not NULL
3. Clear output structure (0x4 to 0x104 bytes)
4. Extract bucket index from hash (hash & 0xFF = 0-255 bucket index)
5. For each bucket from index to 255:
   a. Acquire critical section lock on bucket
   b. Iterate through linked list of items in bucket
   c. Compare item hash against all items in list
   d. If match found, accumulate statistics and copy item data
   e. Release lock and return 1
6. If no match found in any bucket, release lock and return 0

Parameters:
itemHash - Hash value to search for (used to calculate bucket index)
pItemId - Output pointer to receive found item ID
pItemData - Output pointer to receive found item data structure

Returns:
1 if item found with data copied to output
0 if item not found or initialization failed

Special Cases:
- Magic value 0x128 represents expected item data size
- Bucket count fixed at 256 (0x100)
- Each bucket protected by critical section for thread safety
- Item data structure size 0x104 bytes copied on match

functions.name: EnumerateItemMemoryBlocks
functions.comment:
Enumerates all item memory blocks and invokes callback for each item with memory statistics.

Algorithm:
1. Check if item table is initialized (g_dwItemTableInitialized), return error if not
2. Validate callback pointer is not NULL using NEG+SBB test
3. Initialize hash search with size 0x128 and iterator 0
4. Call FindItemByHash to locate first item
5. If items found, enter main loop; otherwise return success with no items
6. For each item: retrieve 3 memory block sizes from fixed offsets
7. Calculate KB values for each block by adding 0x200 offset and shifting right 10 bits
8. Format memory stats using wsprintfA with format string "%s:%d  blocks=%u  %uk/%uk/%uk"
9. Invoke callback with formatted output buffer and context
10. Call FindItemByHash again to find next item
11. Loop until no more items found, then return success

Parameters:
pCallback: Pointer to callback function to invoke for each item (void* for function pointer)
nContext: User-defined context value passed to callback on each invocation

Returns:
1 on success (items enumerated or no items found with valid callback)
0 on initialization error or invalid callback

Special Cases:
- If g_dwItemTableInitialized is 0, immediately returns 0 with error code 0x8510007d
- If g_dwErrorReportingEnabled is set, calls SetLastError() before returning
- Callback validation uses NEG+SBB trick instead of direct NULL check
- Memory block sizes converted to KB units using add/shift pattern

Structure Layout:
Item memory block access pattern (from disassembly):
Offset    Size    Field Name            Type         Description
------    ----    ----------            ----         -----------
0x128     4       nMemBlockSize1        uint         First memory block size in bytes
0x124     4       nMemBlockSize2        uint         Second memory block size in bytes
0x134     4       nMemBlockSize3        uint         Third memory block size in bytes

functions.name: ClearMemoryAndRemoveBlock
functions.signature: void ClearMemoryAndRemoveBlock(void * pHeapHandle, MemoryBlockHeader * pMemHeader, uint dwHeapIndex, void * pAllocationInfo)
functions.comment:
Clears allocated memory block with debug pattern and removes from heap pool.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwConfigBit3 flag from data memory to check if debug clearing is enabled
2. Test flag value and jump to cleanup if zero (clearing disabled)
3. Load flags byte from pMemHeader+0x3 to check skip-clear bit (0x4)
4. Jump to cleanup if bit 4 is set (memory already cleared or special type)
5. Load base block size as word from pMemHeader+0x0
6. Extract bit 0 from flags byte and shift left by 1 to get size adjustment (0 or 2 bytes)
7. Subtract size adjustment from base size
8. Load reserved byte from pMemHeader+0x2 and subtract from size
9. Subtract 8 bytes as header overhead from calculated size
10. Calculate DWORD count by right-shifting size by 2 bits
11. Fill DWORD-aligned portion of pAllocationInfo with 0xdddddddd pattern using REP STOSD
12. Calculate remaining bytes (size AND 3) to fill
13. Fill remaining bytes with 0xdd pattern using REP STOSB
14. Call DeallocateMemoryBlockFromPool to remove block from heap management
15. Return with 8-byte stack cleanup (RET 0x8)

Parameters:
pHeapHandle - Heap identifier or handle (implicit ECX register via __fastcall)
pMemHeader - Pointer to MemoryBlockHeader structure with block size and flags (implicit EDX register via __fastcall)
dwHeapIndex - Index or identifier of heap pool segment (stack parameter)
pAllocationInfo - Pointer to memory region to be cleared with debug pattern (stack parameter)

Returns:
void - Function performs in-place memory clearing and initiates deallocation

Special Cases:
- Memory clearing only occurs if g_dwConfigBit3 is non-zero (debug mode)
- Bit 4 of pMemHeader[3] flags byte indicates skip-clear (may be preformatted)
- 0xdddddddd is standard Windows debug fill pattern for freed allocations
- Size calculation accounts for variable-sized header using adjustment flag
- Remaining bytes after DWORD fill handled separately using byte fill

functions.name: ProcessAndCleanMemoryBlockList
functions.comment:
Processes and validates Storm memory block list by iterating through entries and removing unallocated blocks.

Algorithm:
1. Dereference input parameter to get memory block header pointer
2. Load entry list boundaries (start at +0x1c, end at +0x20)
3. Initialize valid block flag to false
4. For each memory entry from start to end:
   - Load entry size from offset +0x0 (word)
   - Load entry flags from offset +0x3 (byte)
   - Calculate next entry: next = current + size
   - If flags & 0x82 == 0 (valid entry):
     - If flags & 0x40 (allocated): Set valid block flag
   - Else (flags indicate free/corrupt):
     - If flags & 0x40 == 0 (not allocated):
       - Check g_dwDebugModeFlag for output mode
       - If debug mode: Format message with szStormMemoryErrorFormat and OutputDebugStringA
       - If not debug mode: Set error 0x8510007e, check g_dwErrorReportingEnabled, call DisplayErrorAndTerminate
     - Call DeallocateMemoryBlockFromPool to remove entry
5. If valid block found: Return original header pointer
6. If no valid blocks: Unlink first entry, free via VirtualFree, return input parameter

Parameters:
pMemoryBlockListPtr: Pointer to memory block list header (MemoryBlockList structure)
  Contains offset +0x1c (entry list start), +0x20 (entry list end)
  Entry structure: [size:word @ +0][reserved @ +1-2][flags:byte @ +3]

Returns:
int*: Original memory block header if valid blocks remain, else input parameter after memory freed

Special Cases:
- Error code 0x8510007e: Storm memory corruption (never released block)
- Entry flags: 0x82 = corruption/free bits, 0x40 = allocated bit, 0x80 = valid bit
- Uses global g_dwDebugModeFlag to control error output (0 = UI, non-zero = debug log)
- Uses global g_dwErrorReportingEnabled to determine if error UI should be displayed
- VirtualFree flags 0x8000 = MEM_RELEASE (deallocate entire allocation)

functions.name: ValidateHeaderSignature
functions.comment:
Validates header file signature structure and nested signatures.

Algorithm:
1. Test if header pointer parameter is NULL; if NULL and error reporting enabled, store error code 0x85100081 and call SetLastError, then return 0 (failure)
2. If pointer is valid, compare magic signature word at offset -2 from header base; expected value is 0x6f6d; if mismatch and error reporting enabled, store error 0x8510007c and call error handler, then return 0
3. Load flag byte at offset -5 from header base; test bit 1 (0x2); if set and error reporting enabled, call error handler with code 0x8510007a and return 0
4. If bit 0 (0x1) is set in flag byte, load size byte at offset -6 and word at offset -8; calculate nested structure offset as [offset -8] minus [offset -6]; compare word at calculated offset to 0x12b1; if mismatch and error reporting enabled, call error handler with code 0x8510007b and return 0
5. If all validations pass, return 1 (success)

Parameters:
- pHeaderPtr (ECX, void*): Pointer to header structure; function validates signature at offset -2 and flag byte at offset -5
- nReportError (EDX, int): Flag controlling error reporting behavior; non-zero enables error handler calls and SetLastError; zero suppresses error reporting

Returns:
- EAX = 1: Header pointer valid and all signature validations successful
- EAX = 0: Header NULL, magic signature invalid at offset -2, flag validation failed, or nested structure signature invalid

Special Cases:
- Magic signature 0x6f6d at offset -2 (little-endian representation of 'om')
- Flag byte at offset -5 controls validation path: bit 1 (0x2) indicates special flag validation, bit 0 (0x1) indicates nested structure present
- Nested structure validation uses dynamic offset calculation: offset = [base-8] - [base-6]
- Error codes: 0x85100081 (NULL header), 0x8510007c (bad magic), 0x8510007a (flag validation), 0x8510007b (nested structure validation)
- Global configuration flag g_dwValidationErrorReportingEnabled at 0x6fc44d58 can override reporting behavior

functions.name: InitializeMemoryProtection
functions.comment:
Initializes memory protection infrastructure and critical sections.

Algorithm:
1. Load and check initialization flag (g_dwItemTableInitialized) at 0x6fc45168
2. If already initialized (flag != 0), jump to exit to prevent redundant initialization
3. Save volatile registers EBX, ESI, EDI for loop iteration
4. Call ParseConfigurationValue with "Internal" section and "Debug Memory" key to populate output buffer at 0x6fc44d5c
5. Call ParseConfigurationValue with "Internal" section and "Protect Memory" key to populate output buffer at 0x6fc43554
6. Load pointer to InitializeCriticalSection function from g_pfnInitializeCriticalSection at 0x6fc33260
7. Load base address of critical section array (g_PoolCriticalSections) at 0x6fc43558 into ESI
8. Initialize loop counter to 256 (0x100) decimal to process all critical sections
9. Loop: Call InitializeCriticalSection for current critical section at ESI
10. Increment ESI by 0x18 bytes (size of CRITICAL_SECTION structure) to move to next entry
11. Decrement counter and continue loop if more sections remain
12. After all 256 critical sections initialized, mark initialization complete by setting g_dwItemTableInitialized to 1
13. Restore registers and return

Parameters:
None - Function takes no parameters

Returns:
void - Function returns nothing; operates via side effects on global critical sections

Special Cases:
- Critical section array contains exactly 256 entries at 0x6fc43558
- Each CRITICAL_SECTION structure is exactly 0x18 bytes (24 decimal)
- Total critical section array size: 256 * 0x18 = 0x2400 bytes (9216 decimal)
- Initialization flag provides thread-safe one-time initialization protection
- Two configuration keys are parsed but outputs not directly used by this function
- Called from DllMainEntryPoint during DLL initialization

Structure Layout:
CRITICAL_SECTION is 0x18 bytes:
  Offset | Size | Field       | Type   | Description
  -------|------|-------------|--------|------------------------
  0x00   | 4    | DebugInfo   | void*  | Debug info pointer
  0x04   | 4    | LockCount   | int    | Lock count (-1 = unlocked)
  0x08   | 4    | RecursionCount | int | Recursion depth counter
  0x0C   | 4    | OwningThread | HANDLE| Thread that owns lock
  0x10   | 4    | LockSemaphore | HANDLE| Semaphore for synchronization
  0x14   | 4    | SpinCount   | DWORD  | Spin count before blocking

functions.name: ValidateMemoryBlockBySearchKey
functions.signature: int ValidateMemoryBlockBySearchKey(uint dwSearchKey, uint dwReserved, uint pMemoryBlock)
functions.comment: Setting prototype: int ValidateMemoryBlockBySearchKey(uint dwSearchKey, uint dwReserved, uint pMemoryBlock)

functions.name: FreeMemoryBlock
functions.signature: int FreeMemoryBlock(int nHeapId, uint dwParam2, uint * pMemoryBlock)
functions.comment:
Frees a memory block from the heap with comprehensive validation and thread-safe locking.

Algorithm:
1. Verify heap system initialized by checking g_dwItemTableInitialized (error 0x8510007d if invalid)
2. Validate pMemoryBlock pointer is not NULL (error 0x85100081 if null)
3. Check memory block signature 0x6f6d at offset -2 (error 0x8510007c if invalid)
4. Test freed flag (bit 1 at offset -5) to prevent double-free (error 0x8510007a if already freed)
5. Validate realloc flag (bit 0) linked block signature 0x12b1 at calculated offset
6. Check forwarding flag (bit 3) and follow parent pointer if set
7. Extract heap index from word at offset +4, verify it matches nHeapId parameter
8. Acquire critical section lock using heap index
9. Call ClearMemoryAndRemoveBlock to deallocate the memory block
10. Release critical section if index != -1
11. Return 1 on success, 0 on validation failure

Parameters:
- nHeapId (int): Heap identifier that must match memory block header heap ID
- dwParam2 (uint): Unused reserved parameter
- pMemoryBlock (uint*): Pointer to memory block data (points past 2-byte signature header)

Returns:
- 1: Memory block successfully freed and removed from heap
- 0: Validation failed or heap is invalid

Special Cases:
- Error 0x8510007d: Heap system not initialized
- Error 0x85100081: Null pointer provided
- Error 0x8510007c: Invalid memory signature (memory corruption)
- Error 0x8510007a: Memory already freed (double-free attempt)
- Error 0x8510007b: Realloc linked block signature invalid
- Memory header located at pMemoryBlock[-2] (signature 0x6f6d)
- Heap index extracted from pMemBlockHeader->heapSizeField word at offset +4
- Critical section index from pMemBlockHeader at offset +8

functions.name: FreeMemoryBlock
functions.comment:
Searches a memory block linked list and frees the block matching the given ID.

Algorithm:
1. Check if heap is initialized (DAT_6fc45168), return 0 if not
2. Store error code 0x8510007d for uninitialized heap case
3. If config flag set, display fatal error and terminate
4. Extract low byte of blockId as slot index for lookup table
5. Calculate critical section address using (slot_index * 0x18)
6. Enter critical section for thread-safe list access
7. Traverse linked list at DAT_6fc43150[slot_index]
8. For each block entry, compare offset +4 with blockId
9. On match, call ProcessAndCleanMemoryBlocks to destroy block
10. Move to next block (dereference offset +0)
11. Return 1 if block found and freed, 0 if not found
12. Leave critical section before returning

Parameters:
blockId [uint] - Memory block identifier to free (passed in EBP)

Returns:
[uint] - 1 if block was found and freed, 0 if not found or heap error

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 immediately if heap not initialized
- Uses low byte of blockId for slot indexing (& 0xff)
- Critical sections protect linked list traversal
- Only low byte of blockId is significant for slot selection

functions.name: GetCellFileDecompressedSize
functions.signature: int GetCellFileDecompressedSize(int isInitialized, CellFile * pCellFile, int nContextParam)
functions.comment:
Calculates the decompressed size of a CellFile graphic resource.

Algorithm:
1. Verify initialization flag (g_dwItemTableInitialized) is set
2. Validate that pCellFile pointer is not NULL
3. Verify CellFile magic signature (0x6f6d = "mo") at offset -2
4. Load format flags from CellFile offset +3 to determine compression type
5. If format flag 0x2 is set, call ReportAndLogError (compressed format not supported)
6. If format flag 0x1 is set, validate alternate encoding with signature check at calculated offset
7. Check format flag 0x8 to determine if parent link exists
8. If parent link flag set, follow pointer at offset -0xc to parent CellFile structure
9. Check format flag 0x4 to determine if using pre-calculated size
10. If flag 0x4 set, return cached size at offset -0x10
11. Otherwise calculate size: height - (width + offset) where offset is 8 or 10 based on flag 0x1

Parameters:
isInitialized: Non-zero indicates item table is initialized; if 0, returns error 0x8510007d
pCellFile: Pointer to CellFile header structure; must not be NULL and have valid magic
param3: Context parameter passed to error handlers; purpose varies by call site

Returns:
Decompressed size in bytes if successful
-1 on any validation failure or error condition
Sets g_dwLastErrorCode to one of: 0x8510007d (not initialized), 0x85100081 (NULL pointer),
0x8510007c (invalid magic), 0x8510007a (compressed format), 0x8510007b (encoding error)

Special Cases:
CellFile structure uses offset -2 for magic and offset -8 for base address
Format flags control compression, encoding, parent links, and cached size storage
Height dimension stored as word at offset 0, width as byte at offset 2
Calculation accounts for different cell dimensions and encoding variants

functions.name: SMemFree
functions.signature: int SMemFree(void * pMemory, void * pErrorContext, int nErrorCode)
functions.comment:
Deallocates memory blocks with validation and thread-safe cleanup.
Algorithm:
1. Load and validate heap handle from g_dwHeapInitialized, if not set return error
2. Validate pMemory pointer is not NULL, else set error 0x85100081
3. Verify memory signature (0x6f6d magic) at offset -2 from pMemory
4. Check flag bits at offset -5: 0x02 (error), 0x01 (sub-alloc), 0x08 (indirect)
5. If flag 0x02 set, call ReportAndLogError and return 0 (blocked)
6. If flag 0x01 and sentinel 0x12b1 check fails, call ReportAndLogError
7. If flag 0x08 set, dereference pointer at offset -4 for actual header
8. Extract heap index from word at offset +2, shift left 16 bits
9. Enter critical section using g_PoolCriticalSections array
10. Call ClearMemoryAndRemoveBlock to deallocate and update metadata
11. Check if heap index is -1, only leave critical section if valid
12. Return 1 on success, 0 on error
Parameters:
pMemory: void * - Pointer to memory block to deallocate
pErrorContext: void * - Error context pointer
nErrorCode: int - Error code for reporting
Returns:
int - 1 if successful, 0 on error
Special Cases:
Signature 0x6f6d validates allocated blocks. Flag byte controls state: 0x01 (sub-allocation), 0x02 (error condition), 0x08 (indirect reference). Sentinel 0x12b1 validates sub-allocations. Heap index -1 indicates invalid pool. Critical section stride is 0x18 bytes.

functions.name: ProcessAndFreeMemoryBlocks
functions.comment:
Processes and frees unreferenced memory blocks from 256 managed memory block lists.

Algorithm:
1. Check global flag g_dwHeapInitialized to determine if processing needed
2. Clear the flag and initialize loop counter to 256 (0x100)
3. For each of 256 memory block lists:
   - Enter critical section to protect list from concurrent access
   - Clear cleanup counter for current list index
   - Iterate through linked list of memory blocks:
     * Load reference count from block+0x14; if zero, block can be freed
     * Check flags field at block+0x10 and size at block+0x4
     * If flags set and size > 0x7FFFFFFF, log debug message (overflow case)
     * Unlink unreferenced block from list by updating next pointer
     * Free block memory using VirtualFree with MEM_RELEASE flag (0x8000)
     * If reference count non-zero, call ProcessAndCleanMemoryBlockList
   - Leave critical section and delete it
   - Advance to next list (pointer index +4, critical section +24 bytes)
4. Return 1 (success code)

Parameters:
   None - Operates on global memory block arrays (g_dwHeapInitialized, g_PoolCriticalSections, g_pItemHashBuckets, g_dwPoolCleanupFlags)

Returns:
   1 - Always returns success code (1) regardless of whether blocks were processed or freed

functions.name: CreateMemoryHeap
functions.comment:
Creates and initializes a memory heap within the global arena pool system.

Algorithm:
1. Check if heap system is initialized; return 0 if not (system not ready)
2. Validate nReserved parameter is 0; return 0 if non-zero (invalid usage)
3. Align dwDesiredSize to 4KB boundary (0x1000); if remainder exists, add padding
4. Enforce minimum heap size of 4KB; if smaller, set to 0x1000
5. Increment global heap handle counter (g_dwHeapHandleCounter) with overflow handling
6. Calculate bucket index from lower 8 bits of heap handle for arena pool distribution
7. Acquire critical section lock for thread-safe arena pool access
8. Search arena linked list in bucket for matching handle; if found, return existing handle
9. Release and re-acquire critical section for allocation phase
10. Call AllocateAndInitializeMemoryArena to create new arena with computed parameters
11. Release critical section lock
12. Check allocation result; if handle is 0, set error code 0x8 and call error display
13. Return heap handle from g_dwHeapHandleCounter

Parameters:
nReserved [int] - Must be zero; reserved for future use
dwDesiredSize [uint] - Requested heap size in bytes; will be aligned to 4KB page boundary

Returns:
[uint] - Non-zero heap handle on success; 0 on failure with error code set

Special Cases:
- Handle overflow: When counter reaches 0, reset to 0x80000000 to avoid zero handles
- Alignment: Sizes not aligned to 4KB are rounded up; 0 size becomes minimum 4KB
- Error codes: 0x8510007d = system not initialized, 0x57 = invalid parameter, 0x8 = allocation failed
- Critical section: Held during arena search and allocation to prevent concurrent modifications
- Bucket distribution: Handle bucketing uses lower 8 bits modulo bucket array size

functions.name: AllocateAndInitializeHeapMemory
functions.comment:
Allocates memory from a heap pool with size validation and optional initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Validate allocation size against maximum limit (0x7fffffff bytes)
2. If size exceeds limit, release critical section and display error, then exit with code 1
3. Verify heap context pointer is non-null
4. Extract and construct allocation control flags from dwFlags:
   - Check bit 0x4000000, if set add flag 0x40 to allocation flags
   - Check bit 0x8000000, if set add flag 0x80 to allocation flags
5. Call AllocateMemoryFromPool with size and constructed flags
6. If allocation succeeds:
   a. If dwFlags bit 0x8 (zero-initialize) is set, fill allocated memory with zeros using optimized STOSD/STOSB
   b. If g_dwConfigBit3 is set (debug mode), fill memory with 0xee pattern using MemSet
   c. Return pointer to allocated memory
7. If allocation fails, release critical section if held
8. If heap context is invalid or allocation failed, display error and exit with code 1

Parameters:
  dwFlags [ESP+4]: Allocation control flags (uint)
    Bit 0x8: Zero-initialize memory after allocation
    Bit 0x4000000: Set allocation flag 0x40 in pool allocator
    Bit 0x8000000: Set allocation flag 0x80 in pool allocator
  dwSize [ESP+8]: Number of bytes to allocate (uint)

Returns:
  void*: Pointer to allocated memory on success
  Never returns on failure (calls ExitProcess(1))

Special Cases:
  - Maximum allocation size: 0x7fffffff (2GB limit)
  - Critical section management: Uses g_PoolCriticalSections indexed by pCriticalSectionIndex
  - Error reporting: Uses DisplayErrorAndTerminate with context from heap structure
  - Memory initialization: Uses optimized REP STOSD for 4-byte chunks then REP STOSB for remainder
  - Debug pattern: 0xee fill controlled by g_dwConfigBit3 flag for uninitialized memory tracking

Structure Layout:
Heap Context (void* pHeapContext):
  Offset  Size  Field Name           Type      Description
  +0x5c   4     dwCriticalSectionId  dword     Critical section identifier for synchronization
  +0x60   n     szErrorMessage       char[]    Null-terminated error message string

functions.name: AllocateMemoryFromArena
functions.signature: void * AllocateMemoryFromArena(uint dwAllocationSize, void * pUnused, int nArenaMode, uint dwPoolSize)
functions.comment:
Allocates memory from a pooled arena structure with synchronization
Algorithm:
1. Check if heap initialization complete (g_dwHeapInitialized flag)
2. If not initialized, initialize heap with error handler configuration
3. Compute hash of arena mode/type from arenaMode parameter
4. Extract arena mode ID from lower 8 bits of hash
5. Calculate critical section address from arena mode (stride of 24 bytes)
6. Enter critical section to synchronize arena pool access
7. Get arena pool list from g_pArenaPoolArray indexed by mode
8. Search linked list for arena matching computed hash
9. If arena not found, allocate new arena via AllocateAndInitializeMemoryArena
10. Allocate memory from arena heap via SMemHeapAlloc
11. Check if new arena was allocated different from previous pool
12. Exit critical section if mode != 0xFF
13. Check cleanup flag g_pMemoryPoolCleanup and clean pools if needed
14. Return allocated memory pointer in EAX

Parameters:
- dwAllocationSize: Size in bytes to allocate
- pUnused: Unused parameter (reserved)
- arenaMode: Arena mode/type identifier (0-255 valid, 0xFF = skip unlock)
- dwPoolSize: Initial pool size for new arena allocation

Returns:
- EAX: Pointer to allocated memory block, NULL if allocation failed

functions.name: ReallocateMemoryBuffer
functions.signature: void * ReallocateMemoryBuffer(void * pOldBuffer, int nOldSize, void * pNewBuffer, uint dwRequestedSize, byte bFlags)
functions.comment:
Allocates or reallocates a memory buffer with optional data copying and padding.

Algorithm:
1. Load flags byte from buffer descriptor at offset +0x3
2. Test external buffer flag (0x4) to determine buffer location
3. If external flag clear (internal buffer):
   a. Load header base size from descriptor offset +0x2
   b. Add 8 byte base offset (10 if bit 0x1 set for size adjustment)
   c. Load total size from descriptor offset +0x0 (ushort)
   d. Calculate available space by subtracting header size from total
4. If external flag set, load available size from pNewBuffer[-4]
5. If buffer is internal and request fits in available space:
   a. Attempt grow-in-place allocation via AllocateMemoryBlock
   b. If successful, set pAllocatedBuffer to pNewBuffer and proceed to fill
6. If grow-in-place fails or request exceeds available:
   a. Check no-allocation flag (0x10)
   b. If set, return NULL immediately
7. Allocate new buffer from heap via AllocateAndInitializeHeapMemory
8. If allocation successful, old buffer not empty, and request valid:
   a. Calculate copy size as minimum(availableSize, dwRequestedSize)
   b. Copy data via CopyMemoryBuffer
9. Cleanup old buffer via ClearMemoryAndRemoveBlock
10. If new allocation failed, return NULL
11. If buffer allocated and fill needed (dwRequestedSize > availableSize):
    a. Check zero-fill flag (0x8); if set use 0x00, else check g_dwConfigBit3
    b. If g_dwConfigBit3 set, use pattern 0xeeeeeeee; if clear skip fill
    c. Calculate fill size as dwRequestedSize - availableSize
    d. Fill dwords using REP STOSD (fill size >> 2 dwords)
    e. Fill remaining 0-3 bytes using REP STOSB (fill size & 3 bytes)
12. Return pAllocatedBuffer (new buffer or reallocated buffer)

Parameters:
  pOldBuffer: Old/source buffer descriptor pointer (implicit in ESI)
  nOldSize: Size parameter for old buffer operations
  pNewBuffer: Target buffer or destination for allocation
  dwRequestedSize: Requested allocation size in bytes
  bFlags: Control flags - 0x04 (external buffer), 0x08 (zero fill), 0x10 (no alloc)

Returns:
  Pointer to allocated/reallocated buffer on success
  NULL on allocation failure or if flag 0x10 set and grow-in-place unavailable

Special Cases:
  - Magic number 0xeeeeeeee: Debug fill pattern (uninitialized memory marker)
  - Header size offsets: 8 bytes base + 2 additional if flag 0x1 set
  - g_dwConfigBit3 controls whether fill pattern is applied (debug vs release mode)
  - REP STOSD/STOSB used for efficient bulk memory fill operations

functions.name: AllocateOrReallocateMemory
functions.signature: uint * AllocateOrReallocateMemory(uint * pOldBuffer, uint dwOldSize, uint * pDescriptor, int nErrorContext, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Allocates or reallocates memory with validation and thread-safe critical section protection.

Algorithm:
1. Load g_dwHeapInitialized flag and verify memory system is ready; exit with error if not initialized
2. Test if pOldBuffer is NULL; if NULL, skip to arena allocation (step 14)
3. If pOldBuffer not NULL, verify header signature at offset -2 equals 0x6f6d ("mo")
4. If signature invalid, set error code 0x8510007c, call SetLastError, conditionally call DisplayErrorAndTerminate if g_dwValidationErrorReporting is set
5. If signature valid, read allocation flags at offset -5 (EDI+3 where EDI = pOldBuffer-8)
6. Test flag bit 0x20000000: if set, log error via ReportAndLogError and skip to arena allocation
7. Test flag bit 0x10000000 (marker validation): if set, verify secondary header at calculated offset equals 0x12b1; if mismatch, log via ReportAndLogError
8. Test flag bit 0x8000000 (follow descriptor chain): if set, dereference pOldBuffer[-3] to load next descriptor pointer
9. Extract pool index from descriptor[4] as word value, shift left 16 bits to get offset into pool array
10. Calculate critical section address: base=g_PoolCriticalSections, stride=0x18 per pool, offset=(pool_index*3)*8
11. Enter critical section for this memory pool using Windows API EnterCriticalSection
12. Call ReallocateMemoryBuffer with descriptor, pool offset, pOldBuffer, dwOldSize, and dwFlags
13. Check return value: if not 0xffffffff, exit critical section and return reallocated buffer
14. If pOldBuffer was NULL or validation failed, call AllocateMemoryFromArena with size, descriptor, error context, and allocation flags
15. Return allocated or reallocated buffer pointer to caller

Parameters:
  pOldBuffer: Pointer to existing memory buffer with header structure, or NULL for new allocation. Buffer header contains signature 0x6f6d at offset -2 and allocation flags at offset -5.
  dwOldSize: Size of existing buffer allocation (used in reallocation calculation)
  pDescriptor: Pointer to memory descriptor structure containing pool index at offset +4 (word) for critical section selection
  nErrorContext: Error context code passed to error handlers and logging functions for diagnostic purposes
  dwFlags: Allocation control flags (0x4=external source, 0x8=zero-fill memory, 0x10=no allocation requested)

Returns:
  Pointer to allocated/reallocated memory buffer on success
  NULL (value 0) if allocation failed
  Never returns if g_dwHeapInitialized is uninitialized (calls ExitProcess with code 1)

Special Cases:
  Header signature 0x6f6d ("mo") is mandatory for existing buffers; invalid signature triggers error path
  Flag 0x20000000 indicates invalid allocation state; buffer cannot be reused
  Flag 0x10000000 enables secondary validation; checks offset marker 0x12b1
  Flag 0x8000000 enables descriptor chain following; loads next descriptor from offset -4
  Error codes: 0x8510007d (uninitialized), 0x8510007c (bad signature), 0x8510007b (marker invalid), 0x8510007a (flag error)
  Pool indexing: descriptor word at offset +4 determines which critical section; 128 pools with 0x18-byte spacing
  Critical section array: g_PoolCriticalSections at 0x6fc43558, contains CRITICAL_SECTION structures
  Reallocation may fail (return 0xffffffff); critical section still properly exited in this case

functions.name: SMemHeapReallocate
functions.signature: uint * SMemHeapReallocate(uint heapIndex, uint flags, uint * pExistingBuffer, uint newSize)
functions.comment:
Reallocate or allocate memory on a Storm Memory heap with thread safety.

Algorithm:
1. Check if heap system is initialized via global flag g_dwHeapInitialized
   - If not initialized, display error 0x8510007d and terminate process
2. If pExistingBuffer is NULL, skip validation and call SMemHeapAllocSpecial
3. Validate buffer header magic 0x6f6d at offset -2 from pExistingBuffer
   - If invalid, set error code 0x8510007c and check g_dwValidationErrorReporting
   - If validation reporting enabled, display error and terminate
4. Check bit 0x2000000 in buffer flags (offset +0xc from base, byte bit 1)
   - If set, skip all validation checks and proceed to reallocation
5. Check bit 0x1000000 in buffer flags (offset +0xc from base, byte bit 0)
   - If set, validate secondary header magic 0x12b1 at adjusted offset
   - If mismatch, call ReportAndLogError with code 0x8510007b
6. Check bit 0x8000000 in buffer flags (offset +0xc from base, byte bit 3)
   - If set, follow pointer chain at offset -0xc to get actual buffer pointer
7. Get heap ID from word at [buffer + 0x4], shift left 16 bits for table offset
   - Load heap index from global heap table at calculated offset and compare with heapIndex parameter
   - If mismatch, return NULL (buffer allocated from different heap)
8. Enter critical section for heap via EnterHeapIndexCriticalSection
9. Call ReallocateMemoryBuffer with critical section handle and reallocation parameters
10. If heapIndex is not 0xffffffff, leave critical section via LeaveCriticalSection
11. Return reallocated buffer pointer

Parameters:
  heapIndex (uint): Index of target heap (0-0xffffff, 0xffffffff = special no-lock case)
  flags (uint): Allocation flags (bit 0-25 = configuration bits)
  pExistingBuffer (uint*): Optional pointer to existing buffer to reallocate, NULL for new allocation
  newSize (uint): Requested buffer size in bytes

Returns:
  uint*: Pointer to reallocated/allocated buffer on success, NULL on failure
         Returns NULL if pExistingBuffer exists but heap ID doesn't match

Special Cases:
  Error 0x8510007d: Heap not initialized (FATAL - process terminates)
  Error 0x8510007c: Invalid buffer header magic (may be fatal if g_dwValidationErrorReporting set)
  Error 0x8510007b: Secondary header validation failed (logged but continues)
  Heap index 0xffffffff: Special case with no critical section locking
  Buffer bit 0x8000000: Indicates buffer is in pointer chain, follow at offset -12
  Buffer bit 0x2000000: Skip all header validations, proceed directly to reallocation
  Buffer bit 0x1000000: Requires secondary header validation with magic 0x12b1

Thread Safety:
  Uses EnterHeapIndexCriticalSection before reallocation
  Uses LeaveCriticalSection after reallocation (except for heap index 0xffffffff)
  Critical sections stored at g_PoolCriticalSections with stride 0x18 per heap

functions.name: DecompressRLEImageData
functions.signature: void DecompressRLEImageData(uint destOffset, int srcBytesRemaining, byte * pDestBuffer, byte * pSrcBuffer, uint imageWidth, uint scanlineWidth, int bytesPerPixel)
functions.comment:
Decompresses run-length encoded (RLE) image data from source to destination buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize destination and source buffer boundary addresses
2. Read bytes from source buffer sequentially (main_loop_start)
3. For literal bytes (< 0xC0): copy to destination at appropriate pixel format offset
4. For RLE bytes (>= 0xC0): extract 6-bit count, read next byte as fill value
5. Dispatch fill operation based on pixel format (1-byte, 3-byte RGB, or generic stride)
6. Handle scanline wrapping when pixel counter exceeds scanline width
7. Continue until source exhausted or destination filled

Parameters:
destOffset (EDX): Initial offset into destination buffer (fastcall register)
srcBytesRemaining (stack +0x28): Remaining bytes in source buffer from current position
pDestBuffer (stack +0x2c): Pointer to start of destination buffer
pSrcBuffer (stack +0x38): Pointer to current position in source buffer
imageWidth (stack +0x3c): Total width of image in pixels
scanlineWidth (stack +0x40): Number of pixels per scanline (may differ from imageWidth)
bytesPerPixel (stack +0x44): Bytes per pixel (1=grayscale, 3=RGB, other=generic stride)

Returns: void

Special Cases:
- RLE marker: byte >= 0xC0 indicates RLE encoding
- RLE count: Lower 6 bits (0x3F mask) specify number of pixels to fill
- Maximum RLE count: 63 pixels per run (6-bit limit)
- Count clamping: Clamps to remaining destination space to prevent overruns
- Pixel formats: Optimizes for common 1-byte and 3-byte formats, generic fallback
- Scanline wrapping: Manages pixel counter and stride when pixels wrap to next scanline
- Buffer boundaries: Validates both source and destination bounds before each access

functions.name: DecodePNGImageData
functions.signature: uint DecodePNGImageData(byte * pPNGData, int * pImageWidth, uint dwDataLength, uint * pPixelBuffer, byte * pPaletteData, uint dwBufferSize, int * pImageHeight)
functions.comment:
Decodes PNG image data, extracting dimensions and converting pixel format from 24-bit RGB to 32-bit RGBA.

Algorithm:
1. Parse PNG header to extract image bounding box coordinates (X-start, X-end, Y-start, Y-end at offsets +0x4, +0x8, +0x6, +0xA)
2. Calculate image width = (X-end - X-start) + 1 and height = (Y-end - Y-start) + 1
3. Extract bit depth factor from header offset +0x3 and palette stride from offset +0x41, compute imageBitDepth = depth * stride
4. Write extracted dimensions to output pointers: width to pImageWidth, height to output parameter at ESP+0x24, bit depth to pImageHeight (null-safe)
5. If pPaletteData pointer valid, call DecompressRLEImageData to decompress palette from PNG offset +0x80
6. If pPixelBuffer valid and imageBitDepth equals 8, convert 256 pixels from source offset nDataLength-0x2fe:
   - Copy 3-byte RGB triplets to destination buffer at pPixelBuffer+2
   - Pad each pixel to 4 bytes RGBA format (set alpha=0x00)
   - Iterate 256 times, advancing source by 3 bytes and destination by 4 bytes
7. Return 1 (success indicator)

Parameters:
  pPNGData     - Pointer to PNG file buffer containing header and image data (required)
  pImageWidth  - Output: pointer to store calculated image width in pixels (null-safe)
  nDataLength  - Total length of PNG data buffer in bytes
  pPixelBuffer - Output: pointer to receive 32-bit RGBA pixel data (null-safe)
  pPaletteData - Output: pointer to receive decompressed palette data (null-safe)
  nBufferSize  - Size of output pixel buffer in bytes, used to validate decompression size
  pImageHeight - Output: pointer to store imageBitDepth value (null-safe)

Returns:
  1 - Function always returns success indicator

Special Cases:
  - All output pointers are null-safe; function validates before writing
  - Pixel conversion only occurs if imageBitDepth == 8 (8-bit indexed color)
  - PNG structure assumes fixed offsets; format must match expected binary layout
  - Pixel data source address calculated dynamically: pPNGData + (nDataLength - 0x2fe)

PNG Format Structure (inferred):
  Offset  Size  Description
  0x00    2     Magic/signature
  0x03    1     Bit depth component value
  0x04    2     Left/X-start coordinate (little-endian)
  0x06    2     Top/Y-start coordinate (little-endian)
  0x08    2     Right/X-end coordinate (little-endian)
  0x0A    2     Bottom/Y-end coordinate (little-endian)
  0x41    1     Palette stride/scaling factor
  0x42    2     Palette height parameter
  0x80    var   Palette data RLE compressed
  var     var   Pixel data (source at nDataLength - 0x2fe)

functions.name: EncodePixelDataRLE
functions.comment:
Encodes pixel data using run-length encoding (RLE) compression for bitmap output.

Algorithm:
1. Load first input byte (address in [EDI]), increment input pointer, decrement remaining count
2. Initialize run length counter to 1 (CL register)
3. If remaining count reaches 0, skip to reserved byte check
4. Enter run detection loop: compare current byte (DL) with next byte at [EAX]
5. If bytes differ OR run length >= 0x3F (63), exit loop to encode
6. Otherwise increment run length, decrement count, advance input pointer
7. Continue loop if bytes remain (ESI > 0)
8. Check if run length >= 2 (CMP ECX, 1; JG): single bytes skip RLE encoding
9. If run length >= 2 OR byte value >= 0xC0, write RLE header: (runLength | 0xC0)
10. Write the byte value to output buffer [EBX]
11. Update output buffer pointer
12. Repeat from step 1 until all input bytes processed (ESI == 0)

Parameters:
EAX (implicit) - Number of input bytes to encode (remainingByteCount)
EDI (implicit) - Pointer to input buffer pointer (pInputBufferPtr) - modified during encoding
EBX (implicit) - Pointer to output buffer pointer (pOutputBufferPtr) - modified during encoding

Returns:
void - No return value. Encodes data in-place via register pointers.

Special Cases:
- Reserved value 0xC0 and above: written with RLE header even if run length is 1
- Run length maximum: 0x3F (63 bytes) due to 6-bit encoding in flag byte
- RLE encoding format: (count | 0xC0) flag byte followed by repeated byte value
- Input/output pointers are passed via registers and updated by reference
