functions.name: WriteImagePixelData
functions.signature: uint WriteImagePixelData(HANDLE hFile, uint dwImageMode, void * pixelBuffer, int imageWidth, int imageHeight, uint dwBytesPerScanline)
functions.comment:
Writes formatted image pixel data to file with optional palette conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize local buffer structures for image header and palette data (18 + 512 byte header)
2. Check image mode parameter: 0x8 = 8-bit paletted, 0x20 = 32-bit direct color
3. If mode is 0x8: set palette mode flags, prepare for palette conversion
4. If mode is not 0x8: set direct color mode flags, no palette needed
5. Call WriteFile to write initial 18-byte header with format information
6. If mode is 0x8: convert palette from 4-byte BGR format to 3-byte RGB format (256 colors)
7. Call WriteFile to write palette data (0x300 bytes = 768 bytes for converted palette)
8. Calculate scanline size: ((imageWidth + 7) >> 3) * imageWidth bytes per row
9. Compare calculated scanline size with bytesPerScanline parameter
10. If sizes match: write all pixel data at once (contiguous block)
11. If sizes differ: write pixel data row-by-row with bytesPerScanline stride
12. Return 1 (success indicator)

Parameters:
hFile - File handle for writing image data (HANDLE)
imageMode - Image color mode: 0x8 for 8-bit paletted, 0x20 for 32-bit direct (uint)
pixelBuffer - Pointer to pixel buffer containing image data (void *)
imageWidth - Width of image in pixels (int)
imageHeight - Height of image in pixels (int)
bytesPerScanline - Expected bytes per scanline row (uint)

Returns:
uint - Always returns 1 (success code)

Special Cases:
- Mode 0x8: 8-bit paletted color with BGR to RGB palette conversion
- Mode 0x20: 32-bit direct color, no palette conversion
- Palette buffer: 768-byte buffer for converted RGB palette (256 colors * 3 bytes each)
- Scanline mismatch: if calculated size != bytesPerScanline, data written row-by-row
- Width alignment: image width calculations use +7 >> 3 for alignment adjustment

Palette Conversion Format (mode == 0x8):
- Input: 4-byte BGR entries from source palette
- Output: 3-byte RGB entries in palette_buffer (768 bytes total)
- 256 color entries converted with byte reordering: B->R, G->G, R->B

functions.name: DecompressImageData
functions.signature: int DecompressImageData(byte * pCompressedData, DCXImageFormatHeader * pImageHeader, int nCompressedSize, byte * pDecompressedBuffer)
functions.comment:
Decompresses bitmap image data from compressed format into raw pixel buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Extract image header metadata: color depth (bits/pixel), width, height from DCXImageFormatHeader
2. Calculate bytes per pixel from bits value: (bits + 7) / 8
3. Calculate uncompressed image size as: bytesPerPixel * width * height
4. Clamp calculated size to available buffer capacity (compressedSize parameter)
5. Extract image orientation flags from header byte at offset +0x11:
   - Bit 4 determines horizontal flip (affects pixel stride direction)
   - Bit 5 determines vertical flip (affects starting row position)
6. Calculate pixel strides and row padding based on orientation:
   - Horizontal flip negates the pixel stride (right-to-left instead of left-to-right)
   - Vertical flip adjusts row stride and starting buffer position (bottom-up instead of top-down)
7. Load compression type from header byte at offset +0x2
8. Switch on compression type to handle different decompression paths:
   - Type 1-2: Uncompressed bitmap data (direct copy with possible orientation adjustment)
   - Type 9-10: RLE (Run-Length Encoded) compressed data with header byte mode encoding
9. For uncompressed types: validate data fits within compressed buffer, copy pixels handling variable color depths (1-4 bytes per pixel), apply orientation transformations
10. For RLE types: parse RLE stream byte by byte, switching between literal run mode (byte < 0x80) and repeat run mode (byte >= 0x80)
11. In literal run mode: count = (byte & 0x7f) + 1, copy that many pixels from stream sequentially
12. In repeat run mode: count = (byte & 0x7f) + 1, copy the next single pixel that many times
13. Handle color depths in inner loops with fall-through switch for 1/2/3/4 byte copies
14. Manage output row positioning using pixelRowStride for pixel advancement and pixelRowStride for row boundaries
15. Validate RLE stream never exceeds compressed data bounds (return 0 on overflow)
16. Return 1 on successful decompression, 0 on any buffer overflow or invalid data

Parameters:
  pCompressedData: Pointer to compressed image data or RLE stream (fastcall ECX register)
  pImageHeader: Pointer to DCXImageFormatHeader structure with color depth, dimensions, and orientation flags (fastcall EDX register)
  compressedSize: Size of compressed data buffer in bytes (fastcall EAX register, passed on stack)
  pDecompressedBuffer: Output pixel buffer for decompressed image data (passed on stack)

Returns:
  int: 1 = Decompression successful, image fully decompressed into buffer
       0 = Decompression failed (RLE stream overflow, buffer too small, invalid compression type)

Special Cases:
  - Fast path optimization: uncompressed images without flipping call CopyMemoryBuffer directly for performance
  - RLE encoding uses high bit as mode indicator: 0x80-0xff = repeat run, 0x00-0x7f = literal run
  - Color depth supports 1-4 bytes per pixel with fall-through switch statement for partial byte copies
  - Image orientation transformations: horizontal flip negates stride sign, vertical flip inverts row order
  - Boundary validation: RLE stream position checked against compressed data end pointer on every run
  - Row transitions: special pixelRowStride applied when completing each scanline (rowPixelWidth pixels processed)

Image Header Structure (DCXImageFormatHeader):
  Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type    | Description
  -------|------|------------------|---------|------------------------------------------
  +0x0c  | 2    | imageWidth       | WORD    | Pixel width of decompressed image
  +0x0e  | 2    | imageHeight      | WORD    | Pixel height of decompressed image
  +0x10  | 1    | bitsPerPixel     | BYTE    | Color depth: 8, 16, 24, or 32 bits
  +0x11  | 1    | orientationFlags | BYTE    | Bit 4=horizontal flip, Bit 5=vertical flip
  +0x02  | 1    | compressionType  | BYTE    | 1=raw, 2=raw, 9=RLE, 10=RLE

functions.name: ValidateAndCopyImageBuffer
functions.signature: int ValidateAndCopyImageBuffer(void * this, undefined1 * param_1, int param_2, undefined4 * param_3)
functions.comment:
Validates DCX image buffer size and converts image pixel data to 32-bit output format.

Algorithm:
1. Extract width (WORD at offset +3) and height (WORD at offset +5) from DCXImageFormatHeader
2. Extract format byte (BYTE at offset +7) and calculate stride in bytes: (format + 7) >> 3
3. Calculate row count as (height - width) for pixel dimension validation
4. Compute expected buffer size: rowCount * dwStrideInBytes
5. Compare computed size with nExpectedSize parameter; if mismatch, return 0 (validation failure)
6. If validation passes, initialize output buffer: clear DWORDs 0 to (dwImageWidth * 4) bytes with zeros
7. Clear remaining BYTE entries up to full stride alignment using REP STOSB
8. If nRowsToProcess > 0, begin pixel copy loop at validation_passed label
9. For each row: read source bytes (3-4 per pixel based on stride) and write as 4-byte DWORDs
10. Stride encoding: stride <= 3 = RGB (3 bytes + 1 zero pad), stride == 4 = RGBA (4 bytes with alpha)
11. Advance source pointer by dwStrideInBytes, destination by 4 bytes per pixel, decrement row counter
12. After all rows copied, zero-pad output buffer from current position to index 256
13. Return 1 on successful validation and conversion

Parameters:
  this: Implicit ECX context pointer - Image object context (unused in this function)
  pImageDesc: Pointer to DCXImageFormatHeader containing width, height, format fields
  pbSourceData: Source image pixel data pointer in stride-encoded format
  nExpectedSize: Expected size in bytes for validation (must equal rowCount * stride)
  pdwOutputBuffer: Pointer to 256-entry DWORD output buffer for converted image

Returns:
  1 if size validation passes and pixel data conversion succeeds
  0 if computed size != nExpectedSize (validation failed)

Special Cases:
  - Output buffer is always 256 DWORDs = 1024 bytes total
  - Stride calculation: format byte is in bits, convert to bytes via (format + 7) >> 3
  - Dimension validation: rowCount = height - width (special calculation, not standard height)
  - Pixel format: stride determines RGB vs RGBA conversion (stride < 4 = RGB + zero pad)
  - Padding: unused entries from end of data to 256 are cleared with zero DWORDs

functions.name: ExtractFileNameFromPath
functions.comment:
Extracts filename from a full file path string.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input path string is not NULL; if NULL, set error 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)
2. Scan forward through path string character by character
3. When backslash (0x5C) separator found, skip to character after it
4. Repeat step 3-4 for all backslash separators (handles nested paths)
5. Once all backslashes processed, focus on filename portion
6. Scan filename for period (0x2E) to locate file extension
7. Return pointer to filename start (after last backslash)
8. If period found in filename, continue scanning through extension
9. Error handling: Set error code 0x57 and call SetLastError on invalid input

Parameters:
pPathString: Input path string in format like C:\path\to\file.ext

Returns:
char*: Pointer to filename portion (after last backslash), or NULL on error
       Calls SetLastError(0x57) for invalid input

Special Cases:
- NULL/invalid input triggers ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (0x57)
- Multiple nested backslashes are handled iteratively
- Paths without extensions still return filename portion
- Global g_dw_lastErrorCode stores error state
- Global g_pfnSetLastError points to Windows SetLastError function

functions.name: WriteGifBitsToAccumulator
functions.comment:
Accumulates bits into GIF LZW encoder buffer and flushes complete bytes to output stream.

Algorithm:
1. Shift input bitCount left by current bit position to align for merge into accumulator
2. OR shifted bits into accumulator field at encoder state +0xc
3. Add bitCount to bit position counter at state +0x10
4. If bit position < 8, return (insufficient bits for byte output)
5. Enter flush loop: extract low byte from accumulator at state +0xc
6. Increment byte counter at state +0x30 and store byte to block buffer at state +0x34
7. If byte counter exceeds 254, trigger block flush to output stream
8. Copy accumulated block bytes from state +0x34 to output buffer via rep movsd/movsb
9. Advance output buffer pointer by byte count
10. Reset byte counter to 0 after flush completes
11. Shift accumulator right 8 bits and decrement bit position by 8
12. Loop back if bit position still >= 8 (more bytes to extract)
13. Compare uncompressed size counter with expansion threshold at state +0x24
14. If threshold exceeded, increment code length counter at state +0x00
15. If code length reaches 12 bits, set mask to 0x1000; else compute (2^bits - 1)

Parameters:
bitCount (EDX implicit): Number of bits to write to accumulator (0-12 range)
IMPLICIT in EAX: pGifEncoderState - Pointer to GIF encoder state with buffer at +0x34

Returns:
void (no return value, modifies encoder state in-place)

Special Cases:
GIF blocks limited to 254 bytes data + 1 byte header. Bit extraction via right shift and AND.
Code length expansion triggered when uncompressed size exceeds threshold at offset +0x24.
Maximum code length is 12 bits (4096 LZW codes). Uses non-standard fastcall with implicit EAX param.

functions.name: CopyBitmapRowsReverse
functions.signature: void CopyBitmapRowsReverse(uint dwNumRows, byte * pDestBuffer, int nDestPitch, int nSrcPitch, byte * pSrcBuffer, int nRowByteWidth)
functions.comment:
Copies bitmap image data rows in reverse order (bottom-up) with pitch-based memory layout.

Algorithm:
1. Validate all input parameters (null pointers and zero pitch/width values)
2. Calculate starting source row address as pSrcBuffer + (numRows-1)*rowByteWidth
3. Set destination row pointer to pDestBuffer
4. Loop for each row (numRows iterations):
   a. Calculate effective byte count as minimum(srcPitch, rowByteWidth)
   b. Copy bytes from source row to destination row using REP MOVSD (4-byte chunks)
   c. Copy any remaining 0-3 bytes using REP MOVSB (single-byte copies)
   d. Decrement row counter and move to next row (source pointer moves backward by rowByteWidth)
5. Return after all rows copied; validation failure sets error code 0x57

Parameters:
- numRows (ECX): Number of bitmap rows to copy (must be non-zero)
- pDestBuffer (EDX): Pointer to destination buffer (must be non-null)
- destPitch (Stack+4): Bytes per row in destination (must be non-zero)
- srcPitch (Stack+8): Bytes per row in source (must be non-zero)
- pSrcBuffer (Stack+C): Pointer to source buffer (must be non-null)
- rowByteWidth (Stack+10): Bytes to copy per row (must be non-zero)

Returns:
- void: No explicit return value; errors trigger SetLastError(0x57) [ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER]

Special Cases:
- Parameter validation uses NEG/SBB pattern to check for null/zero values
- Error code 0x57 indicates invalid parameter (null pointer or zero size)
- Rows copied in reverse order (bottom-up), typical for Windows BMP format
- Uses REP MOVSD/MOVSB for efficient bulk memory copy
- Handles non-aligned row widths by copying remainder bytes individually

Structure Layout:
Bitmap data uses pitch-based row layout where each row may be padded:
Offset  Size   Field          Description
------  ----   -----          -----------
0       pitch  row_0          First row (dest) or last row (src when reversed)
pitch   pitch  row_1          Second row
...
n       pitch  row_n          Last row (dest) or first row (src when reversed)

functions.name: DecodeBMPImageData
functions.signature: int DecodeBMPImageData(uint * pOutImageWidth, uint * pOutImageHeight, int pBMPData, uint * pOutputBuffer, int nOutputSize)
functions.comment:
Decodes BMP image data and extracts metadata from BMP file header.

This function processes BMP (Bitmap) image files by reading image dimensions and color depth from the BMP header structure, optionally copying raw bitmap scanline data to an output buffer with byte-swapping for proper channel ordering, and finally decompressing the image data using a helper function. It validates input parameters and handles the conversion of BMP's native byte layout to the application's expected format.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pOutImageWidth pointer non-null; if valid, extract image width at offset +0x12 and store to *pOutImageWidth
2. Validate pOutImageHeight pointer non-null; if valid, extract image height at offset +0x16 and store to *pOutImageHeight
3. Validate pBMPData pointer non-null; if valid, extract color bit depth at offset +0x1c and store to *pBMPData as 16-bit value
4. Load bit depth value from offset +0x1c and compare against threshold 0x8 (9 bits)
5. If bit depth >= 9 (unsupported), clear pBMPData to skip data copy; otherwise continue
6. If pBMPData is non-null and bit depth < 9, copy raw bitmap data with byte reordering:
   - Source: BMP header offset +0x36 (raw scanline data)
   - Destination: pBMPData buffer
   - Loop 256 iterations (0x100 counter)
   - Each iteration copies 4 bytes with pattern: src[+1], src[+0], src[-1], null terminator
   - Advances source by +4, destination by +4 per iteration
   - Total: 256 * 4 = 1024 bytes copied with channel reordering
7. If pOutputBuffer is non-null, calculate uncompressed bitmap size:
   - Formula: (bitDepth * width * height) >> 3 (divide by 8 for bytes)
   - Check alignment: if size & 0x3 != 0, align to 4-byte boundary by adding (4 - (size & 0x3))
8. Call CopyBitmapRowsReverse() with decompression parameters
9. Return 1 (success code)

Parameters:
pOutImageWidth (Stack[0x4]) - Output pointer for image width in pixels; writes DWORD at this address if non-null
pOutImageHeight (Stack[0x8]) - Output pointer for image height in pixels; writes DWORD at this address if non-null
pBMPData (Stack[0xc]) - Input pointer to BMP raw bitmap data buffer; reads from header+0x36 and writes to this buffer if non-null
pOutputBuffer (Stack[0x10]) - Output buffer for decompressed image data; receives decompressed bitmap if non-null
nOutputSize (Stack[0x14]) - Size of output buffer in bytes; passed to decompression function

Returns:
1 - Success code (always returns 1 regardless of parameter validity)

Special Cases:
Magic Numbers:
  0x36 - Offset from BMP header start to raw bitmap scanline data
  0x12 - Offset to image width field (little-endian DWORD at header+0x12)
  0x16 - Offset to image height field (little-endian DWORD at header+0x16)
  0x1c - Offset to bit depth/color count field (little-endian WORD at header+0x1c)
  0x100 - Loop iteration count (256 scanlines max, 4 bytes each = 1024 total)
  0x8 - Threshold for bit depth validation (9 bits); values >= 9 skip data copy
  0x3 - Alignment mask for checking 4-byte boundary

Structure Layout (BMP Header):
Offset  Size  Field           Type      Description
0x00    2     bfSignature     ushort    Magic number (0x4D42 = "BM")
0x02    4     bfSize          uint      Total file size in bytes
0x06    4     bfReserved      uint      Reserved area (typically 0)
0x0A    4     bfOffsetBits    uint      Offset to bitmap data start
0x12    4     biWidth         uint      Image width in pixels
0x16    4     biHeight        uint      Image height in pixels (signed for top-down)
0x1c    2     biBitCount      ushort    Color bit depth (1,4,8,16,24,32)
0x36    ...   bitmapData      byte[]    Raw scanline data starts here

functions.name: ProcessImageFormatDispatcher
functions.signature: int ProcessImageFormatDispatcher(int nFormatType, short * pImageData, uint dwDataLength, void * pOutputBuffer, byte * pOutputData, int nOutputMode, uint * pOutSize1, uint * pOutSize2, uint * pOutSize3)
functions.comment:
Image format dispatcher that validates input and routes to format-specific handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize output size pointers to 0 if non-null (pOutSize1, pOutSize2, pOutSize3)
2. Validate input parameters: Check that pImageData is non-null AND nDataLength > 0
3. Perform secondary validation based on nOutputMode: if mode is 0 then pOutputData must be non-null
4. If validation fails, set global error code to 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and return 0
5. If nFormatType is 0 (auto-detect mode) and nDataLength >= 2, read magic number from first word
6. Detect format type by comparing magic number:
   - 0x50A: Type 1 (format with 0x50A signature)
   - 0x4D42: Type 2 (BMP format with 'BM' signature)
   - Other values: Calculate type as (value != 0x4D42) * 2 + 1, resulting in 1 or 3
7. Dispatch to appropriate handler based on format type:
   - Type 1: Call DecodeBMPImageData to process format
   - Type 2: Call DecodePNGImageData to process PNG/similar format
   - Type 3: Call ValidateDCXImageHeader to process DCX format
8. Return handler result or 0 if dispatch fails

Parameters:
nFormatType: Format code (0=auto-detect, 1-3=explicit type)
pImageData: Pointer to image data buffer containing format signature
nDataLength: Size of data buffer in bytes (must be >= 2 for auto-detect)
pOutputBuffer: Output buffer for format-specific processing results
pOutputData: Output data area for decoded/processed content
nOutputMode: Mode flag controlling output behavior (0=certain mode)
pOutSize1: Pointer to output size/status value 1 (may be NULL)
pOutSize2: Pointer to output size/status value 2 (may be NULL)
pOutSize3: Pointer to output size/status value 3 (may be NULL)

Returns:
int: 0 if validation fails or dispatch fails, otherwise returns value from handler function

Special Cases:
- Error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) set for validation failure
- Magic number 0x50A indicates format type 1 (legacy format)
- Magic number 0x4D42 is 'BM' in ASCII (BMP format signature)
- Type 0 with invalid data length skips auto-detect (uses explicit type)
- Type values outside 1-3 range result in return value 0

functions.name: FindOrInsertHashEntry
functions.comment:
Finds or inserts color code entry in GIF encoding hash table using linear probing collision resolution.
This function manages a circular hash table with 4987 entries used during LZW compression for GIF encoding.
It handles hash collisions via backward linear probing with wraparound, automatically resetting the table
when entry count exceeds the 4096-entry limit to clear collision chains and restart with small codes.

Algorithm:
1. Check pending write flag at context+0x18; if set, store paletteIndex at context+0x14 and return
2. Calculate initial hash index: (paletteIndex * 16) + context[0x14], wrap modulo 0x138b
3. Read code value from context[0x28] (code table) at calculated hash index
4. Create hash key combining indices: (context[0x14] << 8) | paletteIndex
5. If code slot occupied (non-zero):
   - Check if stored hash key at context[0x2c] matches current hash key
   - If match, update context[0x14] and return (entry already exists)
   - If no match, calculate probe distance: 1 if index==0 else (0x138b - index)
   - Linear probe backward: decrement index by probe distance with wraparound at 0
   - Continue probing until empty slot or matching hash key found
6. For new entry (empty slot after probing or initial probe):
   - Call GifBitBufferWrite to output current code
   - Check if entry count at context[0x24] exceeds 0x1000 (4096)
   - If exceeds: reset table, increment reset counter, call output, restore code width
   - If not full: store entry count at code table, increment count, store hash key
7. Update context[0x14] to paletteIndex
8. Return

Parameters:
  pCodeValue: int* - Pointer to output code buffer (passed to GifBitBufferWrite callback)
  paletteIndex: uint - Palette index value (0-255) to find or insert into hash table

Returns:
  void - No return value; updates GIF compression context with new/existing code

Special Cases:
  - Hash table holds 0x138b (4987) entries in circular buffer
  - Table resets when 0x1000 (4096) entries filled to clear collision chains
  - Linear probing searches backward from hash position for collision resolution
  - EBX register implicitly holds pointer to GIF context throughout function

functions.name: WriteBitmapHeaderAndPixelData
functions.signature: uint WriteBitmapHeaderAndPixelData(HANDLE hFile, int * pSrcPalette, int imageHeight, int imageWidth)
functions.comment:
Writes BMP file header and RLE-encoded pixel data to file.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize 128-byte BMP header structure with zeros (32 DWORDs)
2. Set BMP header magic value (0x50A), format flags (1-bit per pixel), and 8-bit color depth
3. Decrement imageHeight and imageWidth by 1 for BMP coordinate system
4. Write BMP header (128 bytes) to output file via WriteFile
5. Allocate pixel buffer: size = imageWidth * imageHeight * 2 bytes (16-bit working buffer)
6. Loop through each image row (imageHeight iterations):
   - Call EncodePixelDataRLE() to RLE-encode current pixel line
   - Decrement row counter until all rows processed
7. Calculate actual encoded pixel data size (buffer_end - buffer_start)
8. Write encoded pixel data to file via WriteFile
9. Deallocate pixel buffer using memory arena
10. Convert source palette from 4-byte BGRA format to 3-byte BGR format:
    - Loop exactly 256 times through palette entries
    - Read 4-byte BGRA chunks from pSrcPalette (offset by +2)
    - Write 3-byte BGR triplets to output buffer (discarding alpha channel)
11. Write palette data (769 bytes total: 1 byte size header + 768 bytes palette) to file
12. Return success code (1)

Parameters:
hFile - File handle for writing output (HANDLE)
pSrcPalette - Pointer to source color palette in BGRA format (int*)
imageHeight - Image height in pixels (int)
imageWidth - Image width in pixels (int)

Returns:
uint - Success indicator (always returns 1 for success)

Structure Layout:
BMP Header (128 bytes at ESP+0x20):
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type        Description
0x00    2     bmpHeaderMagic          word        Magic value 0x50A
0x02    1     formatFlag              byte        Format indicator (always 1)
0x03    1     colorDepth              byte        Color depth in bits (8)
0x04    2     headerWidthMinusOne     word        Image width - 1
0x06    2     headerHeightMinusOne    word        Image height - 1
0x08    2     reserved_0x48_1         word        Constant 0x48
0x0A    2     reserved_0x48_2         word        Constant 0x48
...rest of header (unused fields set to 0)

Special Cases:
- Pixel buffer size: imageWidth * imageHeight * 2 (allocated as 16-bit working buffer)
- Palette conversion: reads offset +2 from pSrcPalette for each 4-byte entry (BGRA skipping alpha)
- Palette size: always 256 color entries (0x100), resulting in 768 bytes of BGR data
- Palette output format: 1-byte size prefix (0x0C) + 768 bytes BGR triplets = 0x301 bytes total
- Memory allocation: uses g_pImageMemoryArena with allocation codes 0x4eb (alloc) and 0x4f2 (free)

functions.name: WriteImageDataToFile
functions.signature: uint WriteImageDataToFile(HANDLE hFile, int imageHeight, int imageWidth)
functions.comment:
Writes a BMP (bitmap) image file with 256-color palette and pixel data.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 1072-byte stack buffer for BMP headers and palette data
2. Write BMP file header (14 bytes): magic 0x4d42 ("BM"), file size, offsets
3. Write DIB info header (40 bytes): width, height, color planes, compression
4. Convert source palette from BGR to RGB format (256 colors, 4 bytes each)
5. Write palette to file (1024 bytes total for 256-entry palette)
6. Align image width to 4-byte boundary for scanline padding calculation
7. Allocate pixel buffer: (aligned_width * height) bytes from memory arena
8. Call CopyBitmapRowsReverse to process and flip pixel rows vertically
9. Write processed pixel data to file
10. Free allocated pixel buffer memory
11. Return success indicator (1)

Parameters:
hFile - File handle for writing output (HANDLE)
imageHeight - Image height in pixels (int)
imageWidth - Image width in pixels (int)

Returns:
uint - Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:
- Palette conversion: BGRX format (BGRx) in source becomes RGBX (RGBx) in output
- Width alignment: scanline width padded to 4-byte boundary per BMP spec
- Pixel buffer: allocated from g_pImageMemoryArena with tag 0x294
- Memory cleanup: buffer freed immediately after WriteFile call

Structure Layout:
BMP File Header (14 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field Name           Type        Description
  0x0     2     bfType              WORD        Magic "BM" (0x4d42)
  0x2     4     bfSize              DWORD       Total file size
  0x6     2     bfReserved1         WORD        Reserved (0)
  0x8     2     bfReserved2         WORD        Reserved (0)
  0xa     4     bfOffBits           DWORD       Offset to pixel data (0x436)

DIB Header (40 bytes):
  Offset  Size  Field Name           Type        Description
  0x0     4     biSize              DWORD       Header size (0x28)
  0x4     4     biWidth             LONG        Image width
  0x8     4     biHeight            LONG        Image height
  0xc     2     biPlanes            WORD        Color planes (1)
  0xe     2     biBitCount          WORD        Bits per pixel (8)
  0x10    4     biCompression       DWORD       Compression type (0)
  0x14    4     biSizeImage         DWORD       Pixel data size
  0x18    4     biXPelsPerMeter     LONG        Horizontal DPI
  0x1c    4     biYPelsPerMeter     LONG        Vertical DPI
  0x20    4     biClrUsed           DWORD       Palette entries (256)
  0x24    4     biClrImportant      DWORD       Important entries (256)

functions.name: WriteGifImageDataToFile
functions.signature: uint WriteGifImageDataToFile(int imageWidth, void * pImageData, int imageHeight)
functions.comment:
Writes GIF87a format image data with color palette to file.
Algorithm:
1. Allocate stack buffer (792 bytes) for GIF header and downsampled pixel data
2. Build GIF87a header: "GIF87a" signature, image width/height in words, packed byte 0xf7, background color 0x00, aspect 0x00
3. Write 13-byte GIF header to file via WriteFile function pointer
4. Downsample 32-bit RGBA to 24-bit RGB via loop: 256 iterations copying 4 bytes to 3 bytes per iteration yields 768-byte output
5. Write 768-byte downsampled pixel data to file
6. Write image data separator 0x2c marking end of image descriptor block
7. Build palette header: logical screen width/height words, packed byte 0x0800, background color, aspect ratio
8. Write 10-byte palette header to file
9. Allocate palette buffer (width*height*2 bytes) from g_pImageMemoryArena via AllocateMemoryFromArena
10. Encode palette data via EncodeGifImageData function call
11. Write encoded palette data block to file
12. Deallocate palette buffer via DeallocateMemoryBlock
13. Write block terminator 0x00
14. Write GIF trailer 0x3b marking file end
15. Return success code 1
Parameters:
  imageWidth: Image width in pixels (signed 32-bit integer)
  pImageData: Pointer to source image pixel data buffer
  imageHeight: Image height in pixels (signed 32-bit integer)
Returns:
  1: Write operation succeeded

functions.name: Ordinal_326
functions.signature: uint Ordinal_326(LPCSTR pFilePath, int nPixelDataSize, void * pPixelData, int nImageWidth, int nImageHeight, int nPixelFormat, uint nDataSizeBytes)
functions.comment:
Writes image data to file in multiple formats (BMP, PCX, PNG, TGA).

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters: file path, pixel data pointer, image dimensions (width/height > 0)
2. Check pixel format validity: if format 0x8 (BMP), pixel data size must be 0
3. Retrieve current image format string via FUN_6fc22710 (format selector callback)
4. For known format (non-BMP): validate format is 0x8, 0x18, or 0x20 (BMP, PCX, TGA)
5. If nDataSizeBytes is 0: calculate buffer size = ((format + 7) / 8) * width
6. Create file handle via CreateFileA with GENERIC_WRITE (0x40000000), CREATE_ALWAYS (2)
7. Match format string and dispatch to handler:
   - BMP: call FUN_6fc22c00 with pixel size param
   - PCX: call FUN_6fc23070 with height param
   - TGA/PNG: call FUN_6fc22170 with full parameters
   - Default: call FUN_6fc22ec0 for generic write
8. Close file handle and return result

Parameters:
  pFilePath - Pointer to null-terminated file path string
  nPixelDataSize - Size of pixel data in bytes (0 for BMP format)
  pPixelData - Pointer to pixel buffer data
  nImageWidth - Image width in pixels (must be > 0)
  nImageHeight - Image height in pixels (must be > 0)
  nPixelFormat - Image format code: 0x8=BMP, 0x18=PCX, 0x20=TGA
  nDataSizeBytes - Output buffer size in bytes (auto-calculated if 0)

Returns:
  Result from format-specific writer function on success (typically 0 for success)
  0 on parameter validation failure (error code 0x57 set)
  INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE (-1) if file creation fails

Special Cases:
  Error 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) set via SetLastError for invalid inputs
  BMP format (0x8) ignores pixel data size, auto-calculates based on format
  Unknown formats dispatch to default TGA writer (FUN_6fc22ec0)

functions.name: SaveScreenCaptureToFile
functions.signature: uint SaveScreenCaptureToFile(LPCSTR lpFilePath, void * pGraphicsBuffer, void * pGraphicsContext, int nWidth, int nHeight, int nBitsPerPixel)
functions.comment:
Saves screen capture/screenshot to file by wrapping WriteImageDataToFile with standard save mode.

Algorithm:
1. Load all six parameters from stack: file path, buffer pointer, graphics context, width, height, bits per pixel
2. Reorganize parameters to match WriteImageDataToFile calling convention
3. Push additional mode flag parameter (0) indicating standard file save operation
4. Call WriteImageDataToFile with all seven arguments to perform actual file I/O and image encoding
5. Return control to caller with automatic stack cleanup (RET 0x18 removes 6 parameters)

Parameters:
- lpFilePath (LPCSTR): Null-terminated path string for output file (e.g., "C:\screenshot.pcx")
- pGraphicsBuffer (void*): Pointer to graphics pixel buffer containing image data to save
- pGraphicsContext (void*): Graphics context or device handle for image format information
- nWidth (int): Image width in pixels (typical range 320-1024)
- nHeight (int): Image height in pixels (typical range 240-768)
- nBitsPerPixel (int): Color depth: 8 for paletted, 16 for 16-bit, 24 for 24-bit RGB

Returns:
- uint: Status code from WriteImageDataToFile (0=failure, non-zero=success with file bytes written)

Special Cases:
- Mode flag parameter (0) indicates standard persistent file save (not preview or temporary)
- File format determined by WriteImageDataToFile based on extension and bit depth
- Buffer and context pointers validated before file I/O by WriteImageDataToFile
- Width/height must be positive to produce valid image file

functions.name: LoadAndParseImageFile
functions.signature: uint LoadAndParseImageFile(byte * pFilePath, uint pOptionalParam, uint pImageBuffer, uint pImageWidth, uint pImageHeight, uint pImageDepth, uint requestedDepth, void * pMemAllocFunc)
functions.comment:
Loads image file from disk, decodes image data, and allocates memory for the decoded buffer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate all output parameters (pImageWidth, pImageHeight, pImageDepth, pImageBuffer)
2. Validate input file path pointer and retrieve game flags from g_dwGameFlags
3. Open and validate game file using OpenAndValidateGameFile
4. Enter critical section for thread-safe file access (g_hFileCriticalSection)
5. Determine file size: use handle offset +0x10c if valid, otherwise read from offset +0x114
6. Allocate temporary buffer in image memory arena (g_pImageMemoryArena)
7. Read file data into temporary buffer
8. Detect image format by reading magic number:
   - 0x050A = PNG format, calls DecodePNGImageData
   - 0x4D42 = BMP format, calls DecodeBMPImageData
   - Other = DCX format, calls ValidateDCXImageHeader
9. Calculate decompressed image size: width * height * depth
10. Check if requestedDepth is satisfied; use decoded depth if requested is 0
11. Allocate output buffer via custom allocator (pMemAllocFunc) or default arena
12. Decode image data into output buffer with proper stride calculation (divide by 8 bits)
13. Copy output parameters (pImageWidth, pImageHeight, pImageDepth) to caller
14. Release file handle and exit critical section
15. Cleanup and return success (1) or failure (0)

Parameters:
szFilePath: Pointer to null-terminated file path string for image file to load
nOptionalFlags: Optional flags for file loading behavior (unused in current implementation)
pImageBuffer: Pointer to output pointer where decoded image buffer address will be stored
pImageWidth: Pointer to DWORD where decoded image width will be written
pImageHeight: Pointer to DWORD where decoded image height will be written
pImageDepth: Pointer to DWORD where decoded image depth will be written
nRequestedDepth: Requested color depth (0 = use detected depth from file)
pMemAllocFunc: Optional custom memory allocator function pointer (NULL = use default)

Returns:
1 on successful image load and decode, 0 on failure or invalid parameters

Special Cases:
Magic numbers: PNG (0x050A), BMP (0x4D42), DCX (all others)
File size calculation: 0x10c offset in handle = file size, 0x114 = alternative size pointer
Image size stride: Calculated as (width * height * depth + 7) / 8 for bit-aligned allocation
Error code 0x57: Invalid parameter error, stored in g_dwLastErrorCode
Depth validation: If requestedDepth specified (non-zero), must match decoded depth exactly
Critical section: g_hFileCriticalSection ensures thread-safe file access during decode

functions.name: ProcessType2BitmapStream
functions.signature: uint ProcessType2BitmapStream(void * this, int param_1, int param_2, undefined4 param_3, int * param_4, int * param_5)
functions.comment:
Decompresses Type 2 bitmap stream and converts pixel format.

Algorithm:
1. Read 0x80-byte metadata header containing bitmap bounds (minX, minY, maxX, maxY) and format byte
2. Extract bitmap width from bounds: width = maxX - minX + 1
3. Extract bitmap height from bounds: height = maxY - minY + 1
4. Calculate total pixel data size: bytesPerPixel * height
5. Determine if format is 8-byte by comparing calculated size to 8
6. Handle no output buffer case: set up stream position and return early
7. For file-based streams, seek to file_size - 0x300 bytes or adjust memory position
8. Allocate temporary transformation buffer with appropriate size
9. Read compressed image data into temporary buffer
10. Decompress data using RLE decompression and pixel format transformation
11. Free temporary buffer after decompression
12. For 8-byte format: read 0x300 bytes of palette/pixel data
13. Convert each 3-byte RGB triplet to 4-byte RGBA with zero alpha channel
14. Return 1 on success, 0 on metadata read failure

Parameters:
  pStreamContext (implicit this): Stream context with file handle, position, and buffer state
  pPixelStream: BitStream pointer for output pixel destination (optional)
  dwOutputBuffer: Address of decompressed pixel buffer (optional)
  dwDataBuffer: Data buffer address
  dwDataSize: Size of data buffer
  pOutputWidth: Pointer to receive calculated bitmap width value
  pOutputHeight: Pointer to receive calculated bitmap height value

Returns:
  1: Processing completed successfully
  0: Metadata read failed or critical error occurred

Special Cases:
  Memory-based streams use handle value -1 with internal memory pool position tracking
  File-based streams use Win32 file handles with SetFilePointer/GetFileSize
  0x300 (768) byte offset used as cache boundary for stream positioning
  8-byte format triggers 3-byte to 4-byte pixel expansion with alpha=0
  Critical section guards protect stream state during position manipulation

functions.name: ReadAndProcessBitmapStream
functions.signature: uint ReadAndProcessBitmapStream(void * this, int param_1, undefined4 * param_2, undefined4 param_3, undefined4 * param_4)
functions.comment:
Reads and processes bitmap/image data from a structured stream format.

Algorithm:
1. Read 14-byte stream header via ReadDataToBuffer (magic bytes, metadata)
2. Read 40-byte stream header containing image dimensions and color depth
3. Extract and validate image metadata: width, height, color bit depth
4. If color bit depth <= 8: Read 1024-byte palette data and transform palette entries
   - Transform 256 entries with byte rearrangement (4 bytes per entry)
5. If image buffer pointer provided: Calculate file offset for decompression
   - Offset = (fileStreamOffset - 0x36) minus 0x400 if decompression needed
6. Synchronize file pointer access using critical section for thread safety
7. If using internal position tracker (ESI+0x10C == -1):
   - Adjust position tracker with bounds clamping to stream size
   - Clear cache fields at ESI+0x138 and ESI+0x13C
8. Otherwise: Use system SetFilePointer to position file handle for read
9. Allocate read buffer (size variable) via AllocateMemoryFromArena
10. Read stream data into buffer via ReadDataToBuffer with byte count tracking
11. Calculate output row byte width: (bitDepth * imageWidth / 8) aligned to 4-byte boundary
12. Call CopyBitmapRowsReverse to decompress/transform image pixel data
13. Free allocated buffer via DeallocateMemoryBlock
14. Verify all expected bytes were read; return 1 (success) or 0 (failure)

Parameters:
  this (ECX): Implicit context pointer for bitmap stream object
  pStreamContext: Pointer to stream context data (possibly BitStream object)
  pImageBuffer: Output buffer for transformed image pixel data (NULL to skip decompression)
  pBytesRead: Output pointer for count of bytes read from stream
  flags: Processing control flags
  pImageMetadata: Output pointer for image metadata structure

Returns:
  1: Success - all headers read, data processed, byte counts match
  0: Failure - header read failed, validation failed, or incomplete read

Special Cases:
  - Bit depth > 8: Skip palette transform loop, use fileStreamOffset directly
  - NULL pImageBuffer: Skip 1024-byte palette read and decompression
  - Internal position tracker (ESI+0x10C == -1): Use clamped position arithmetic
  - Negative file offsets: Handled via NEG/SBB for sign extension
  - Row alignment: Output buffer padded to 4-byte boundary per CopyBitmapRowsReverse
  - File positioning: Critical section protects file pointer manipulation

Structure Layout - BitStream Object (ESI):
  Offset 0x10C (4 bytes): File handle (-1 if using internal tracker)
  Offset 0x114 (4 bytes): Pointer to stream size array
  Offset 0x11C (4 bytes): Internal position tracker (when handle is -1)
  Offset 0x138 (4 bytes): Cache invalidation flag 1
  Offset 0x13C (4 bytes): Cache invalidation flag 2

functions.name: ValidateAndDecodeBitmapStream
functions.signature: int ValidateAndDecodeBitmapStream(void * pStreamHandle, byte * pOutputBuffer, uint dwReserved, uint * pOutWidth, uint * pOutHeight, uint * pOutBitDepth)
functions.comment:
Validates bitmap stream format and decodes palette and image data

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x420 bytes (1056) stack buffer for temporary header and image data
2. Call ReadDataToBuffer to read 18-byte (0x12) bitmap header from stream
3. Validate read succeeded and header size matches expected 0x12 bytes
4. Call ValidateBitmapImageFormat to parse header fields and extract dimensions
5. Extract header fields: imageWidth (word), imageHeight (word), paletteColorDepth (byte), hasPalette flag (byte)
6. Calculate palette data size: if hasPalette is nonzero, compute ((paletteColorDepth+7)/8) * paletteWidthInPixels
7. Calculate image data size: if compression type < 9 (compressed), compute ((bitDepth+7)/8) * height * width; else 1 byte
8. Call GetStreamFileSize to determine total available stream data
9. Validate file contains enough data: header(0x12) + palette_size + image_size + initial_offset
10. Write output dimensions to caller-provided pointers (pOutWidth, pOutHeight, pOutBitDepth) if provided
11. Enter critical section (g_CriticalSectionGameSync) to synchronize access to stream offset cache
12. Check if stream is file-based or in-memory by examining file handle field (offset +0x10c)
13. If file-based: use SetFilePointer to position file pointer to start of palette/image data
14. If in-memory: adjust internal offset cache at +0x11c, clamp to stream bounds [0, streamEnd-1]
15. Leave critical section after offset positioning
16. If palette flag set and output stream valid: read palette data, call ValidateAndCopyImageBuffer to decode palette
17. If output image buffer provided: allocate temporary buffer, read compressed image data, call DecompressImageData to decode
18. Free temporary buffer on success (flag 0x120) or failure (flag 0x11d)
19. Return 1 on success, 0 on any validation/parsing/decode failure

Parameters:
pStreamHandle: Pointer to BitStream structure containing file handle, offset cache, size info
pOutputBuffer: Optional buffer to receive decoded image pixel data
reserved: Unused parameter (reserved for future compatibility)
pOutWidth: Optional pointer to receive decoded image width in pixels
pOutHeight: Optional pointer to receive decoded image height in pixels
pOutBitDepth: Optional pointer to receive decoded bits-per-pixel value

Returns:
1 if stream validation succeeded and data decoded successfully (or validation-only if no output buffers)
0 if read failed, header invalid, file size insufficient, format parsing failed, or decode failed

Special Cases:
- If hasPalette is 0x00, palette size is zero and palette decode phase is skipped
- If paletteColorDepth is 0, palette calculation yields 0 bytes
- If compression type is >= 9, indicates uncompressed image (1 byte only, stream positioning)
- If stream offset calculation underflows (negative), offset is clamped to 0
- Stream offset is always clamped to max(0, streamEnd - 1) to prevent out-of-bounds access
- Temporary decode buffers allocated from memory arena with source file path szSourceFilePathSBMP

4. Loop through nodes comparing IDs at offset +0x8

functions.name: ProcessMultipleHashTables
functions.comment:
Updates four related hash tables with a key value across multiple hash table identifiers.

Algorithm:
1. Load dwTableKey parameter from stack into ESI
2. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5348 and dwTableKey
3. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5349 and dwTableKey
4. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d534a and dwTableKey
5. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5347 and dwTableKey
6. Return 1 to indicate successful completion

Parameters:
- dwTableKey (uint): The key value to lookup and update in all four hash tables

Returns:
- uint: Always returns 1 (success code) regardless of individual hash table operations

Special Cases:
- The four magic identifiers (0x534d5348, 0x534d5349, 0x534d534a, 0x534d5347) represent
  four related but distinct hash tables that all maintain the same key
- The function updates all four tables atomically as a batch operation
- Return value is constant (always 1) suggesting this operation never fails

functions.name: ProcessExceptionFrame
functions.comment:
Finds and removes an exception frame from the exception frame list and hash tables.

Algorithm:
1. Compare provided exception frame ID with cached ID value
2. If IDs match, clear the cached ID and load the main exception frame list head
3. Validate the list head pointer is not null
4. Initialize exception frame pointer from list head
5. Loop through the linked list comparing each frame's ID (offset +0x8) with the target ID
6. When matching frame found, remove it from 4 hash tables:
   - Remove with hash key 0x534d5347
   - Remove with hash key 0x534d5348
   - Remove with hash key 0x534d534a
   - Remove with hash key 0x534d5349
7. Call UnlinkAndRestoreExceptionFrame to deallocate the frame structure
8. Call DeallocateMemoryBlock to free the frame's memory block with size -2
9. Return to caller

Parameters:
  nExceptionFrameId (EBX): Exception frame identifier to locate and remove

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - Cached ID optimization: If provided ID matches cached ID, clears cache and reloads list
  - Empty list handling: If list head is null or negative, function returns early without processing
  - Linked list traversal: Uses offset +0x4 for next pointer, +0x8 for ID comparison
  - Magic hash keys: 0x534d5347, 0x534d5348, 0x534d534a, 0x534d5349 identify hash tables to clean

Structure Layout (Exception Frame):
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  -------|------|-----------|------|-------------
  +0x0   |  4   | Reserved  | dword | Reserved or unused field
  +0x4   |  4   | pNext     | void* | Pointer to next frame in list
  +0x8   |  4   | nFrameId  | uint  | Exception frame identifier

functions.name: ProcessExceptionFrameQueue
functions.comment:
Processes all exception frames in the queue by iterating through the global exception frame linked list and calling the frame processing routine on each node.

Algorithm:
1. Push EDI register to preserve caller's value
2. Load the exception frame queue head pointer from DAT_6fc458e8
3. Check if queue head pointer is valid (> 0)
4. If queue is empty (pointer <= 0), jump to return success
5. Loop through linked list: load current frame node pointer from offset +0x8 of each node
6. Call FUN_6fc24150 to process each exception frame (handles hash table cleanup, unlink, restore)
7. Jump back to step 3 to check next node
8. When queue becomes empty, set EAX to 1 (success), restore EDI, and return

Parameters:
None - operates on global exception frame queue (DAT_6fc458e8)

Returns:
EAX = 1 (success)

Structure Layout:
The function accesses nodes in a linked list with the following layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type        Description
------  ----  ---------------------  -----------  ------------------------------------------
0x0     4     pNextNode               pointer     Pointer to next exception frame node
0x4     4     pPrevNode               pointer     Pointer to previous exception frame node
0x8     4     exceptionFrameId        uint        Exception frame identifier/handle
0xC     ...   additionalFields        ...         Other frame data processed by FUN_6fc24150

Special Cases:
- Empty queue: When DAT_6fc458e8 <= 0, the queue is considered empty and function returns immediately
- Single node: The loop processes one node and then checks again, allowing single-node handling
- The global pointer DAT_6fc458e8 acts as the queue head; each iteration fetches offset +0x8 from current node

functions.name: FilterWindowMessage
functions.signature: LRESULT FilterWindowMessage(HWND hwnd, uint uMsg, uint wParam, LPARAM lParam)
functions.comment:
Window message interceptor and dispatcher for custom message handling.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 8 bytes on stack for local variables (handledFlag, customHandlerOutput)
2. Initialize both local variables to zero via XOR EAX, EAX
3. Call ProcessMessageCallbacks with window handle, message ID, wParam, lParam, 
   and pointers to handledFlag and customHandlerOutput output parameters
4. Test if custom handler returned non-zero in EAX
5. If handler returned non-zero, load handledFlag from stack and test it
6. If both conditions are true, load customHandlerOutput and return it immediately
7. Otherwise, push the four original parameters and call DefWindowProcA for default handling
8. Return the result from DefWindowProcA

Parameters:
- hwnd (HWND): Window handle that received the message
- uMsg (uint): Message identifier (WM_* constant from Windows API)
- wParam (uint): First message parameter (semantic meaning varies by message type)
- lParam (LPARAM): Second message parameter (often pointer to message-specific structure)

Returns:
- LRESULT: Message processing result. If custom handler processed the message
  (returned non-zero with handledFlag=1), returns the custom result. Otherwise 
  returns DefWindowProcA result for default Windows message handling.

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x8: Stack space for 2 DWORD output parameters
- Magic number 0x10: Stack frame cleanup value for RET instruction (4 params × 4 bytes)
- Custom handler delegation pattern: Allows interception of all window messages
  for custom processing before passing unhandled messages to Windows default handler
- This is typical for window subclassing and message hooking scenarios

Structure Offsets (used by ProcessMessageCallbacks internally):
- ESP+0x10: handledFlag output parameter location (initialized/modified by handler)
- ESP+0x14: customHandlerOutput location (initialized/modified by handler)

functions.name: ValidateAndGetFunctionPointer
functions.comment:
Validates a validation mode parameter and returns a function pointer on success.

Algorithm:
1. Load validationMode parameter from stack (ESP+4) into EDX register
2. Test if validationMode equals 0 using TEST EDX, EDX instruction
3. Set AL=1 if mode is non-zero (invalid), AL=0 if mode is zero (valid)
4. Decrement EAX: converts 0 to -1 (valid), 1 to 0 (invalid) for jump condition
5. Jump to valid_return (0x6fc24399) if mode is valid (EAX non-zero)
6. Set global error code: g_dwNetworkErrorCode = 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER)
7. Call g_SetLastErrorProc(0x57) to notify Windows API of validation failure
8. Clear EAX to 0 (NULL pointer) and return from error path
9. Load g_pGameValidationFunction pointer into EAX for valid mode
10. Return function pointer on success or NULL (0) on validation failure

Parameters:
  nValidationMode (int): Mode validation flag. Must be 0 for success; any non-zero value triggers error handling and returns NULL.

Returns:
  int: Returns function pointer (0x6fc24300) on successful validation (nValidationMode==0), returns 0 (NULL) on error when nValidationMode!=0.

Special Cases:
  - Error code 0x57 = ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (standard Windows API error code)
  - Global variable g_dwNetworkErrorCode is set for downstream error tracking and logging
  - Calling convention is __stdcall with RET 0x4 (callee cleans 4 bytes from stack)
  - TEST/SETNZ/DEC sequence provides efficient conditional logic without branches until final validation
  - Function is called from program initialization (Entry Point) to validate startup parameters

functions.name: SetupTlsExceptionHandlerValue
functions.comment:
Initializes and configures a TLS exception handler record with a custom value.

Algorithm:
1. Push EDI register to save caller-save register
2. Push 3 parameters for AllocateAndInitializeTlsExceptionRecord: allocation flags (0), TLS slot offset (0), base address (0x6fc458e0)
3. Move exception handler mode flag (0x2) into EDI register
4. Call AllocateAndInitializeTlsExceptionRecord to allocate and initialize TLS exception record
5. Load exceptionValue parameter from stack at offset +0x8
6. Store exceptionValue into allocated record at offset +0x8 (field index [2] in DWORD array)
7. Restore EDI register
8. Return with stdcall cleanup (4 bytes of parameters)

Parameters:
exceptionValue: DWORD exception handler value to store at offset +0x8 in the TLS exception record

Returns:
void (side effect: configures TLS exception record structure)

Special Cases:
- Uses __stdcall calling convention with callee-cleanup (RET 0x4)
- EDI register is preserved (push/pop) but used to pass mode flag (0x2) to called function
- TLS base address 0x6fc458e0 is hardcoded as global g_InitializedGameObject
- Offset +0x8 represents the third DWORD field in the exception record (0-indexed array element [2])
- Called function AllocateAndInitializeTlsExceptionRecord returns pointer to allocated/initialized exception record in EAX

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name          Type    Description
------  ----  -----------         ----    -----------
0x0     0x4   field_0             DWORD   First DWORD field
0x4     0x4   field_1             DWORD   Second DWORD field
0x8     0x4   exceptionValue      DWORD   Exception handler value set by caller

functions.name: InitializeLinkedNodeThreadSafe
functions.comment:
Allocates and initializes a new linked list node with thread synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock (g_GameCriticalSection) for thread-safe access
2. Call AllocateAndInitializeLinkedNode() to allocate new node from linked list pool
3. Store nodeValue parameter at offset +8 within the allocated node structure
4. Release critical section lock to allow other threads to proceed
5. Return success status code (1)

Parameters:
nodeValue (uint): The value to be stored at offset +8 in the new linked node

Returns:
uint: Always returns 1 to indicate successful node allocation and initialization

Special Cases:
- Critical section is shared with 25 other functions for game-wide thread safety
- Offset +8 in the linked node structure stores application-specific node data
- Function provides no error handling; allocation failure is not detected
- All error handling occurs in AllocateAndInitializeLinkedNode() function

functions.name: RegisterEventHandler
functions.comment:
Registers an event handler in the global event handler linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that dwEventId context parameter is non-null using NEG/SBB validation trick
2. If dwEventId is null, set error code 0x57 via SetLastError and return 0
3. Load global event handler list head pointer from g_pEventHandlerListHead
4. Search the linked list for an existing handler with matching ID at offset +8
5. If handler found, jump to registration phase at handler_found_or_allocated
6. If handler not found, allocate new handler from memory pool via AllocateAndInitializeTlsExceptionRecord
7. Store event ID in the newly allocated handler at offset +8 relative to handler base
8. Call RegisterEventHandlerInHashTable with handler context, event ID, and parameter data
9. Return success status code in EAX register

Parameters:

  dwHandlerParam (Stack +4): Handler parameter data to pass to registration routine
  
Returns:

  - Handler list may be empty (NULL pointer) on first registration attempt
  - Linked list traversal uses offset +4 for next node pointer within handler structure

functions.name: HandleServerMessage
functions.signature: void HandleServerMessage(uint dwMessageId, uint dwMessageType, uint dwMessageData)
functions.comment:
Routes server messages to the main message dispatcher with SMSG protocol identifier.

Algorithm:
1. Extract dwMessageType and dwMessageData from stack parameters (param2 and param3)
2. Push SMSG magic constant (0x534d5347) as first argument to dispatcher
3. Call DispatchObjectRemovalRequest with magic constant, message type, and message data
4. Clean stack and return to caller (stdcall cleanup)

Parameters:

dwMessageType: Message type identifier - passed directly to dispatcher
dwMessageData: Message payload or data reference - passed directly to dispatcher

Returns:

Special Cases:
Magic Constant 0x534d5347 ("SMSG"): Server message identifier that marks packets as server-originated
messageId Parameter: Present in function signature but not referenced - suggests possible future enhancement or compatibility
Unused Register ESI: Saved and restored but not used elsewhere in function

Protocol Notes:
SMSG constant (0x534d5347) is a 4-byte network protocol identifier in big-endian format
__stdcall convention: Callee cleans 12 bytes from stack (3 parameters × 4 bytes)

functions.name: ProcessMultipleHashTables
functions.comment:
Updates four related hash tables with a key value across multiple hash table identifiers.

Algorithm:
1. Load dwTableKey parameter from stack into ESI
2. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5348 and dwTableKey
3. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5349 and dwTableKey
4. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d534a and dwTableKey
5. Call ProcessHashTableEntry with hash identifier 0x534d5347 and dwTableKey
6. Return 1 to indicate successful completion

Parameters:
- dwTableKey (uint): The key value to lookup and update in all four hash tables

Returns:
- uint: Always returns 1 (success code) regardless of individual hash table operations

Special Cases:
- The four magic identifiers (0x534d5348, 0x534d5349, 0x534d534a, 0x534d5347) represent
  four related but distinct hash tables that all maintain the same key
- The function updates all four tables atomically as a batch operation
- Return value is constant (always 1) suggesting this operation never fails

functions.name: ProcessMessageLoop
functions.comment:
Main Windows message processing loop with idle callback support

Algorithm:
1. Initialize callback counter to zero
2. Check for pending messages using PeekMessageA (non-blocking check)
3. If no pending messages and idle callback provided, call it with counter value
4. Idle callback returning non-zero exits idle processing immediately
5. Call GetMessageA to block until a message arrives (or WM_QUIT)
6. If WM_QUIT received (GetMessageA returns 0), check cleanup flag
7. If cleanup flag set, call ShutdownGameAndCleanup to release resources
8. Otherwise translate and dispatch messages to target windows
9. Loop back to check for more pending messages
10. Return message wParam on quit or final idle callback counter

Parameters:
pIdleCallback: Function pointer called when no messages pending; receives counter; return 0 to continue loop, non-zero to exit
bProcessWmQuitCallback: Flag (1=call cleanup, 0=skip); determines if ShutdownGameAndCleanup invoked on WM_QUIT

Returns:
WPARAM from quit message or final idle callback counter value

Special Cases:
Idle callback counter incremented each time invoked with pending messages
Callback counter reset to zero when transitioning from idle to GetMessageA blocking phase
WM_QUIT terminates outer loop and returns immediately

functions.name: SetError
functions.comment:

3. Place the error code back on the stack as the parameter for the next function
4. Jump to SetLastError via an indirect dispatch pointer for API call forwarding

Parameters:

Returns:
void. The function does not return a value to the caller.

Special Cases:
- This function acts as an intermediary between application code and the Windows SetLastError API
- The global g_dwLastErrorCode maintains a cached copy of the last error for local diagnostic purposes
- The SetLastError dispatch is resolved through a function pointer table at 0x6fc331fc

Structure Layout:
This function does not access any structure fields; it only manipulates error codes (DWORD values).

functions.name: LoadResourceString
functions.comment:
Loads a localized string resource from the game resource table with fallback error handling.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve module handle from global at 0x6fc45390 (g_hModuleInstance)
2. Calculate resource ID by adding 0x5100 to resourceErrorIndex in ESI
3. Call LoadStringA API with: handle, resource ID (ESI+0x5100), buffer address (0x6fc45aa0), size (0x100)
4. Test if LoadStringA succeeded (non-zero result in EAX means success)
5. If load succeeded, return pointer to string buffer at 0x6fc45aa0
6. If load failed (EAX=0), fetch fallback error message from error pointer table
7. Index error table at 0x6fc35cb0 using resourceErrorIndex*4 to get error message pointer
8. Return fetched error message pointer or success buffer pointer in EAX

Parameters:
  IMPLICIT ESI: resourceErrorIndex - Error index (0-0xb range) used to locate resource and error fallback
                Resource offset is 0x5100 + resourceErrorIndex

Returns:
  EAX: char* - Pointer to null-terminated error string
               If LoadStringA succeeded: pointer to buffer at 0x6fc45aa0 (256 byte capacity)
               If LoadStringA failed: pointer to error template from table at 0x6fc35cb0[resourceErrorIndex*4]

Special Cases:
  - Resource IDs in range 0x5100-0x510b (0x5100 + errorIndex for indices 0-11)
  - String buffer has fixed capacity of 256 bytes (0x100)
  - Error template table indexed by resourceErrorIndex to provide context-specific error messages
  - Called from DisplayErrorAndTerminate with various error codes (0, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11)
  - Uses __stdcall convention: callee cleans stack

Structure Layout:
  Global Resources:
  Address  Size  Name                       Type        Description
  0x6fc45390  4  g_hModuleInstance         HANDLE      Module/resource handle
  0x6fc45aa0  256 g_szResourceStringBuffer  char[256]   Loaded resource string buffer
  0x6fc33368  4  PTR_LoadStringA           FARPROC     Pointer to LoadStringA API function
  0x6fc35cb0  4+ PTR_s_ERROR...            pointer[]   Error message pointer table (indexed by error code)

functions.name: AppendLinkedListNode
functions.comment:
Appends a new 12-byte node to the end of a global linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Load the global linked list head pointer from g_pMessageListHead at address 0x6fc4537c
2. Test if the list is empty by checking if the head pointer is NULL
3. If the list is not empty, traverse the linked list by following the nextNode pointers located at offset +0x8 in each node until reaching a node with a NULL nextNode pointer
4. Call HeapAlloc with size 0xc (12 bytes) and flags 0x4 (HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY) to allocate memory for the new node
5. Insert the newly allocated node into the list by writing its pointer to the nextNode field (+0x8) of the previously last node
6. Initialize the new node fields: store wNodeValue parameter at offset +0x0, store module instance from g_hModuleInstance at offset +0x4
7. Set the nextNode field (+0x8) of the new node to NULL to mark it as the end of the list
8. Return to caller with __stdcall cleanup

Parameters:
- wNodeValue (ushort): 16-bit identifier value to store at offset +0x0 in the new node

Returns:
- void: No return value. Function modifies the global linked list structure in place.

Special Cases:
- Empty list: If g_pMessageListHead is NULL, the newly allocated node becomes the new head
- Allocation failure: No error checking; function crashes if HeapAlloc fails
- Global state: Modifies global linked list head at 0x6fc4537c and references module instance at 0x6fc45390

Structure Layout (LinkedListNode - 12 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name   Type     Description
------  ----  -----------  -------  ----------------------------------
0x0     0x2   wNodeValue   ushort   Node identifier value
0x2     0x2   reserved     ushort   Padding/alignment
0x4     0x4   pDataPtr     void*    Module instance context pointer
0x8     0x4   pNextNode    void*    Next node pointer (NULL if last)

functions.name: InsertListNode
functions.comment:
Inserts a new message node into a thread-safe linked list.

Algorithm:
1. Atomically increment global initialization counter using InterlockedIncrement
2. If result is 0, this is the first call; initialize critical section for synchronization
3. If result is non-zero, decrement counter back (already initialized by another thread)
4. Enter critical section to obtain exclusive access to the message list
5. Allocate 12 bytes from process heap with HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag (clears allocated memory)
6. Store nodeDataId (ushort) at offset +0 of allocated block
7. Store nodeValue (uint) at offset +4 of allocated block
8. Load current list head pointer from global g_pMessageListHead
9. Store previous head pointer at offset +8 (creates link to old head)
10. Update global g_pMessageListHead to point to newly allocated node (replaces list head)
11. Leave critical section and return success status 1

Parameters:
  nodeDataId (ushort): Data identifier or type tag for this message node
  nodeValue (uint): Associated data value to store with the message

Returns:
  uint: Always returns 1 (success status)

Special Cases:
  - Uses InterlockedIncrement/Decrement for atomic one-time critical section initialization
  - Multiple threads safe: synchronizes access through critical section
  - Allocates exactly 12 bytes (2 + 4 + 4 for id/value/next plus 2-byte alignment padding)
  - List operates as stack (LIFO) with newest nodes inserted at head
  - HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag automatically clears all allocated bytes

functions.name: InitializeThreadSafeStorage
functions.comment:
Initializes thread-safe global storage with two 32-bit parameters and current thread ID.

Algorithm:
1. Call InterlockedIncrement on g_dwInitCounter to atomically increment the counter
2. TEST EAX against 0 to check if this is the first call (counter was 0 before increment, now returns 1 on first call)
3. If not first call (initCallCount != 0): Jump to not_first_call label at 0x6fc1f2ec
4. If first call (initCallCount == 0): PUSH address of g_CriticalSection and CALL InitializeCriticalSection
5. JMP to after_init label at 0x6fc1f2f7 to skip decrement in else branch
6. At not_first_call: PUSH address of g_dwInitCounter and CALL InterlockedDecrement to undo the increment
7. At after_init: PUSH address of g_CriticalSection and CALL EnterCriticalSection
8. Load dwFirstParam from stack (ESP+0x4) into EAX
9. Load dwSecondParam from stack (ESP+0x8) into ECX
10. MOV EAX to global storage at g_dwFirstParameter (0x6fc42fd4)
11. MOV ECX to global storage at g_dwSecondParameter (0x6fc42fd8)
12. CALL GetCurrentThreadId to retrieve current thread ID into EAX
13. MOV EAX to global storage at g_dwThreadId (0x6fc42fdc)
14. PUSH address of g_CriticalSection and CALL LeaveCriticalSection
15. RET 0x8 to return and pop 2 parameters from caller stack

Parameters:
dwFirstParam (uint): First 32-bit parameter value to store in g_dwFirstParameter at offset 0x6fc42fd4
dwSecondParam (uint): Second 32-bit parameter value to store in g_dwSecondParameter at offset 0x6fc42fd8

Returns:
void - No return value; stack cleaned by callee (RET 0x8)

Special Cases:
- First concurrent call initializes g_CriticalSection; InterlockedIncrement ensures only one caller does this
- Subsequent concurrent calls skip initialization but still decrement counter via InterlockedDecrement
- All calls store their parameters and current thread ID in protected globals within critical section
- Uses __stdcall calling convention: callee pops parameter stack (RET 0x8 for 2 dword params)

functions.name: ExtractAndCopyUniversalName
functions.comment:
Extracts and copies components from a universal name string (format: ".U*domain*server")
Algorithm:
1. Validate input string length (minimum 6 characters required)
2. Verify string starts with ".U" prefix (bytes 0-1 check for '.' at offset 0, 'U' at offset 3)
3. Locate first separator using strpbrk to find delimiter characters
4. Extract domain portion between first and second separators
5. Strip trailing underscores from extracted domain by scanning backward
6. Copy processed domain to three separate global output buffers (g_pOutputBuffer1, g_pOutputBuffer2, g_pOutputBuffer2)
7. Return 1 on success, 0 on any validation failure

Parameters:
pUniversalName (char*): Universal format string to parse (e.g., ".U*domain*server")

Returns:
EAX: 1 if successfully parsed and copied, 0 if validation failed (invalid format or missing separators)

Special Cases:
- Handles underscore suffix removal by null-terminating before underscores
- Minimum string length check prevents buffer overruns
- Multiple consecutive underscores are all stripped
- If second separator not found, returns failure (0)

Universal Name Format:
Offset 0: '.' (literal dot)
Offset 1: 'U' (literal U)
Offset 2-3: '*' separators used to delimit domain and server parts
Example input: ".U*DOMAIN_*SERVER"
Extracted: "DOMAIN" (underscores removed)

functions.name: InitializeResourceLists
functions.comment:
Initializes three resource linked lists for game data management.

Algorithm:
1. Call AppendLinkedListNode with resource type ID 0x510
2. Call AppendLinkedListNode with resource type ID 0x876
3. Call AppendLinkedListNode with resource type ID 0x878
4. Return from function

Parameters:
  (No parameters) - This function takes no parameters

Returns:
  void: Function modifies the global linked list head at g_pMessageListHead by appending three nodes

Special Cases:
  - Resource type IDs 0x510, 0x876, 0x878 are type identifiers for different game resource types
  - Function relies on g_pMessageListHead being initialized to NULL before first call
  - Function relies on g_hModuleInstance containing a valid module instance pointer

functions.name: FormatSystemMessage
functions.signature: bool FormatSystemMessage(DWORD messageId, LPSTR outputBuffer, DWORD bufferSize)
functions.comment:
Formats a system message by looking up the message ID in a thread-safe registry table and using FormatMessageA to apply parameters.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that outputBuffer is not NULL and bufferSize is greater than 0. If validation fails, set error code 0x57 (ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER) and return false.
2. Atomically increment the initialization counter g_dwInitCounter using InterlockedIncrement to track active threads.
3. If the counter becomes 0 (first thread), initialize the critical section g_MessageListCriticalSection for thread synchronization.
4. If counter was not 0, decrement it using InterlockedDecrement as this is a subsequent thread.
5. Enter the critical section to acquire exclusive access to the message table.
6. If g_dwMessageListInitialized is 0 (first-time initialization), set it to 1 and load three message resources (0x510, 0x876, 0x878) using AppendLinkedListNode.
7. Initialize pMessageResource to NULL and pCurrentNode to point to the head of the message table g_pMessageListHead (linked list).
8. Loop through the message table: for each entry, extract the message ID (upper 16 bits of messageId shifted right by 16 and masked to 12 bits).
9. Compare extracted message ID with the word at offset 0x0 in the current node. If match found, extract the message resource pointer from offset 0x4 and jump to format_message_exit.
10. If no match, follow the next pointer at offset 0x8 and continue searching. If pCurrentNode becomes NULL, exit loop with pMessageResource still NULL.
11. Release the critical section and clear the first character of outputBuffer.
12. Call FormatMessageA with flags (0x1800 if pMessageResource is valid, 0x1000 if NULL), message resource pointer, messageId, 0x400 (FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER), outputBuffer, bufferSize, and NULL varargs.
13. Return the result of FormatMessageA (non-zero indicates success, zero indicates failure).

Parameters:
messageId (DWORD): Message ID to format. Upper 16 bits contain the lookup key (shifted right 16 and masked to 12 bits).
outputBuffer (LPSTR): Pointer to buffer where the formatted message will be stored. Must not be NULL and must have sufficient space.
bufferSize (DWORD): Size of outputBuffer in bytes. Must be greater than 0.

Returns:
bool: Non-zero (true) if FormatMessageA successfully formatted the message. Zero (false) if validation fails or message formatting fails.

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x57: Windows error code ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER for invalid buffer parameters.
- Message ID extraction: Upper 16 bits used (messageId >> 0x10 & 0xfff) to extract 12-bit lookup key.
- FormatMessageA flags: Uses negative boolean conversion (-(pMessageResource != NULL) & 0xfffff800) + 0x1000 to select flags.
- Thread-safe initialization: InterlockedIncrement/Decrement on g_dwInitCounter ensures only first thread initializes critical section.
- Linked list structure: Each node contains [message_id_word (offset 0x0), reserved (offset 0x2), message_resource_ptr (offset 0x4), next_node_ptr (offset 0x8)].

Message List Node Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x0    | 2    | messageId  | word | Message ID (12-bit lookup key in lower bits)
0x2    | 2    | reserved   | word | Reserved/padding
0x4    | 4    | pResource  | ptr  | Pointer to message resource or format string
0x8    | 4    | pNext      | ptr  | Pointer to next node in linked list, or NULL if last node
Total: 12 bytes per node

functions.name: RemoveExceptionHandlersByKey
functions.comment:
Removes all exception handlers matching the specified key from the thread-local exception handler chain.

Algorithm:
1. Increment thread-local initialization counter using InterlockedIncrement
2. If first call (counter == 0), initialize critical section for synchronization
3. Otherwise decrement counter to restore balance
4. Enter critical section to serialize list access across threads
5. Load head of exception handler chain from g_pErrorHandlerCallbackListHead
6. Apply sign-extension mask ((value < 1) - 1 & value) to safely handle NULL/invalid pointers
7. While list contains valid nodes (address > 0):
   a. Compare handler key at node offset +8 with target handlerKey parameter
   b. If match found: save next node pointer, unlink current node, deallocate with sentinel -2, continue with saved next
   c. If no match: advance to next node via offset +4 pointer
8. Leave critical section to release list lock

Parameters:
  handlerKey (int) - Handler identification key; all nodes with matching key at offset +8 are removed

Returns:
  void - No return value; modifies exception handler chain as side effect

Special Cases:
  Critical section synchronization prevents race conditions during multi-threaded access
  Sentinel value -2 passed to deallocate function marks handler as being unregistered
  Sign-extension mask preserves NULL pointer semantics when node value < 1
  Must save next pointer before unlinking to avoid using freed memory
  Handler nodes: offset +4 = next pointer, offset +8 = key, offset +0/+12+ = reserved/context data

Structure Layout (ExceptionFrame Node):
  Offset  Size  Field Name      Type        Description
  +0      4     reserved0       uint        Unknown/reserved field
  +4      4     next_handler    pointer     Pointer to next node in chain
  +8      4     handlerKey      int         Handler identification key to match
  +12+    var   context         varies      Exception context/state data

functions.name: DisplayErrorAndTerminate
functions.signature: uint DisplayErrorAndTerminate(uint errorCode, uint * pErrorData, int errorContext, byte * pOptionalString, int isModal, uint exitCode)
strings:
0x46BE4|s_:_error_%u:_6fc36be4| : error %u: 
0x59F76|pu_Program:_%s_6fc49f76|Program:	%s
0x59F06|pu_This_application_has_encountered_6fc49f06|This application has encountered a critical error:

%s
0x46CC8|s_This_application_has_encountered_6fc36cc8|This application has encountered a critical error:

%s
0x46CB8|s_Program:_%s_6fc36cb8|Program:	%s
functions.comment:
Displays a formatted error message to the user and terminates the application.

Algorithm:
1. Check g_dwProcessTerminationFlag and g_dwErrorHandlerReentryLock; return 0 if already active
2. Initialize module path and module name buffers to empty strings
3. Call GetModuleFileNameA to retrieve full module path
4. Initialize WIN32_FIND_DATA structure and call FindFirstFileA to extract filename
5. Copy filename from find data and close find handle
6. Find last '.' character in filename and truncate extension (null-terminate at dot)
7. Format module-specific prefix string using FormatSystemMessage
8. If FormatSystemMessage fails, load fallback format string and use wsprintfA with error code
9. Check if pErrorData exists and context type is -2 or -3; if so validate with ParseUniversalNameAndCopy
10. Copy validated context data to context buffer, or use pErrorData if validation succeeds
11. If context buffer exists, copy to message buffer at current position
12. If errorContext > 0, append formatted context type string
13. Append formatted error code in format "error: 0xXXXX"
14. Append module name to message
15. Load error message resource template 0x5101, format with module prefix, and append to message
16. Load program name template resource 0x5102, format with full module path, and append
17. Switch on errorContext (-4 to positive) and append appropriate formatted context string
18. Append optional string parameter with special handling for magic value 0x85100000
19. If no optional string provided, use g_szDefaultLocaleFallback
20. Iterate through g_pErrorHandlerCallbackListHead linked list to call all registered error handlers
21. For each handler in list, call with (errorCode, formatBuffer, contextBuffer, errorContext, pOptionalString)
22. If any callback returns 0, skip MessageBox display and jump to display_messagebox label
23. Validate parent window using IsWindow and IsWindowVisible on g_hCurrentGameWindow
24. If window invalid or hidden, set hParentWindow to NULL
25. Call MessageBoxA with message, title, flags based on isModal parameter
26. Leave g_ErrorHandlerCriticalSection
27. If isModal non-zero AND user clicked "Retry" (button 7), clear lock and return 1
28. If user clicked "Cancel" (button 2), call __break to enter debugger
29. Set g_dwProcessTerminationFlag = 1 to prevent recursive error handling
30. Call GetVersion to detect Windows version
31. If NT-based (GetVersion returns negative), validate exit code with GetExitCodeProcess
32. Call TerminateProcess with exitCode parameter
33. Return 0 on normal exit

Parameters:
errorCode (UINT): Error code combining facility and status information; used in formatting messages
pErrorData (UINT*): Optional error context data; used if errorContext is -2 or -3
errorContext (INT): Error classification code (-4 to positive); determines message formatting
pOptionalString (BYTE*): Optional context string; appended with locale fallback handling
isModal (INT): Modal dialog flag; non-zero adds MB_APPLMODAL to MessageBox flags
exitCode (UINT): Process termination exit code if normal flow continues to TerminateProcess

Returns:
UINT: 1 if isModal and user clicked "Retry" button; 0 normally; never returns if user clicks "Cancel"

Special Cases:
